BG.mainDish1Desc: Chopped tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers and onion topped with a thick layer of grated sirene white cheese.
BG.mainDish2Desc: Pork or chicken slow-cooked in a clay pot with onions, peppers, mushrooms and wine.
BG.streetFoodDesc: Flaky filo pastry layered with eggs, yogurt and sirene cheese, sold warm from bakeries for breakfast.
BG.dessertDesc: Rolled filo pastry filled with grated pumpkin, walnuts, sugar and cinnamon.
BG.drinkDesc: Grape or plum fruit brandy sipped with salads, and a salted yogurt-and-water drink.

BY.mainDish1Desc: Grated potato pancakes fried until crisp and served with sour cream.
BY.mainDish2Desc: Stew of pork and sausage in a sour cream gravy, used as a dip for draniki or blini.
BY.streetFoodDesc: Small baked or fried buns filled with cabbage, potato, meat or jam.
BY.dessertDesc: Pan-fried pancakes of farmer's cheese (tvorog), egg and flour, served with sour cream or jam.
BY.drinkDesc: Fermented rye-bread drink, and a honey-and-spice vodka liqueur traditional in Belarus.

HR.mainDish1Desc: Lamb, veal or octopus roasted with potatoes under a bell-shaped iron lid covered in hot embers.
HR.mainDish2Desc: Dalmatian risotto of cuttlefish or squid cooked in its own ink with garlic, olive oil and wine.
HR.streetFoodDesc: Thin Poljica pie filled with Swiss chard, onion and parsley, baked on an open hearth and brushed with garlic oil.
HR.dessertDesc: Small fried dough balls flavoured with rakija, citrus zest and raisins, dusted with sugar.
HR.drinkDesc: Herb-infused grape rakija, and red wine mixed with water.

CY.mainDish1Desc: Large chunks of pork or lamb seasoned with oregano and lemon, slow-roasted on long skewers over charcoal.
CY.mainDish2Desc: Lamb on the bone slow-baked with potatoes, garlic and bay leaves in a sealed clay oven.
CY.streetFoodDesc: Minced pork and onion sausages wrapped in caul fat, grilled and served in pitta.
CY.dessertDesc: Strings of almonds or walnuts dipped repeatedly in thickened grape must and dried.
CY.drinkDesc: Sweet dessert wine from sun-dried grapes, and a clear pomace spirit.

CZ.mainDish1Desc: Marinated beef sirloin in a creamy root-vegetable sauce, served with bread dumplings, cranberries and whipped cream.
CZ.mainDish2Desc: Roast pork with bread dumplings and braised sauerkraut.
CZ.streetFoodDesc: Breaded and deep-fried slab of Edam cheese served in a bun or with tartar sauce.
CZ.dessertDesc: Round yeast pastries topped with poppy seed, plum jam or sweet curd cheese.
CZ.drinkDesc: Pale lager first brewed in Plzeň in 1842, and a herbal bitter liqueur from Karlovy Vary.

DK.mainDish1: Fried Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce
DK.mainDish1Desc: Crisp-fried slices of pork belly served with boiled potatoes and a white parsley sauce; voted Denmark's national dish in 2014.
DK.mainDish2Desc: Pan-fried meatballs of minced pork and veal with onion, served with potatoes and gravy.
DK.streetFoodDesc: Red-dyed boiled pork sausage sold from pølsevogn hot-dog stands with mustard, ketchup and remoulade.
DK.dessertDesc: Cold rice pudding folded with whipped cream, vanilla and chopped almonds, served with warm cherry sauce.
DK.drinkDesc: Caraway- or dill-flavoured grain spirit, and mulled wine with raisins and almonds at Christmas.

EE.mainDish1Desc: Porridge of mashed potatoes and barley groats topped with fried bacon and onion, from the Mulgimaa region.
EE.mainDish2Desc: Blood sausage made with barley and pork, roasted and served with lingonberry jam at Christmas.
EE.streetFoodDesc: Dark rye bread topped with butter, spiced Baltic sprats, boiled egg and herbs.
EE.dessertDesc: Flour of roasted barley, rye, oat and pea mixed with kefir or buttermilk and sweetened with berries or honey.
EE.drinkDesc: Dark rum-based spiced liqueur, and a fermented bread drink similar to kvass.

FO.mainDish1Desc: Leg of mutton wind-dried for months in slatted sheds (hjallur), sliced thin and eaten on bread.
FO.mainDish2Desc: Fermented, partly air-dried mutton, often boiled into a soup or served with potatoes.
FO.streetFoodDesc: Wind-dried fish, usually cod, eaten in strips with butter as a snack.
FO.dessertDesc: Rhubarb porridge of stewed rhubarb thickened with potato starch and served with milk or cream.
FO.drinkDesc: Beer from Föroya Bjór, the Faroese brewery in Klaksvík founded in 1888.

FI.mainDish1Desc: Thin rye crust folded around rice porridge and baked, topped with egg butter (munavoi).
FI.mainDish2Desc: Thinly shaved reindeer meat braised in butter and stock, served with mashed potatoes and lingonberries.
FI.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried doughnut-style pastry filled with minced meat and rice, often split and topped with sausage.
FI.dessertDesc: Cardamom-spiced cinnamon bun sprinkled with pearl sugar.
FI.drinkDesc: Light-roast filter coffee drunk in large quantities, and a gin-grapefruit long drink created for the 1952 Olympics.

AX.mainDish1Desc: Thick oven-baked pancake of semolina or rice porridge flavoured with cardamom, served with prune cream and whipped cream.
AX.mainDish2Desc: Butterflied Baltic herring fillets coated in rye flour and pan-fried, served with mashed potatoes.
AX.streetFoodDesc: Dense, sweet black bread of rye and malt, eaten with butter and herring.
AX.dessertDesc: Stewed prunes thickened into a sweet compote, traditionally served on Åland pancake.
AX.drinkDesc: Beer from Åland's Stallhagen brewery, and juice pressed from apples grown on the islands.

VA.mainDish1Desc: Roman pasta of tonnarelli tossed with Pecorino Romano and black pepper; Vatican City has no cuisine of its own and eats Roman dishes like this.
VA.mainDish2Desc: Roman pasta dressed with egg yolk, guanciale, Pecorino Romano and black pepper, as eaten in Rome and the Vatican.
VA.streetFoodDesc: Roman fried rice croquettes with tomato sauce and a mozzarella centre, sold in pizzerias around the Vatican.
VA.dessertDesc: Roman sweet brioche bun split and filled with whipped cream.
VA.drinkDesc: Strong Italian coffee, and white wine from the Castelli Romani hills near Rome.

HU.mainDish1Desc: Beef soup with onions, potatoes, carrots and plenty of sweet paprika, originally cooked by herdsmen in a kettle.
HU.mainDish2Desc: Chicken braised in a paprika and onion sauce finished with sour cream, served with nokedli dumplings.
HU.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried flatbread rubbed with garlic and topped with sour cream and grated cheese.
HU.dessertDesc: Sponge cake layered with chocolate buttercream and topped with a hard caramel layer, created by József Dobos in 1885.
HU.drinkDesc: Fruit brandy, often apricot or plum, and sweet aszú wine from the Tokaj region.

IS.mainDish1Desc: Soup of lamb on the bone simmered with root vegetables, cabbage and rice or oats.
IS.mainDish2Desc: Fish stew of flaked cod or haddock mashed with potatoes, onion and a white sauce, eaten with rye bread.
IS.streetFoodDesc: Lamb-based hot dog served with raw and fried onions, ketchup, sweet mustard and remoulade.
IS.dessertDesc: Thick cultured skimmed-milk dairy product eaten with berries and cream.

LV.mainDish1Desc: Boiled grey peas mixed with fried bacon and onions, often eaten with kefir.
LV.mainDish2Desc: Potato salad with beetroot, pickles, egg and meat or herring, bound with sour cream and mayonnaise.
LV.streetFoodDesc: Crescent-shaped yeast buns filled with chopped bacon and onion.
LV.dessertDesc: Open rye-dough tart filled with mashed potato and sweetened carrot, spiced with cinnamon.
LV.drinkDesc: Bitter herbal liqueur made in Riga since 1752, and a fermented rye-bread drink.

LI.mainDish1Desc: Small egg-flour dumplings layered with grated sour cheese (Sura Kees) and topped with fried onions, served with apple sauce.
LI.mainDish2Desc: Cornmeal cooked with milk and fried in butter into crumbly pieces, eaten with apple sauce or coffee.
LI.streetFoodDesc: Grilled pork and veal sausage with a bread roll and mustard, as also eaten in neighbouring Switzerland and Austria.
LI.dessertDesc: Apple rings dipped in batter, fried and dusted with cinnamon sugar.
LI.drinkDesc: Red wine from vineyards around Vaduz, including the Prince of Liechtenstein's Hofkellerei.

LT.mainDish1Desc: Large zeppelin-shaped dumplings of grated potato stuffed with minced meat, served with bacon, onion and sour cream sauce.
LT.mainDish2Desc: Cold pink soup of kefir and beetroot with cucumber, dill and egg, served with hot boiled potatoes.
LT.streetFoodDesc: Strips of dark rye bread fried and rubbed with garlic, often served with cheese sauce as a beer snack.
LT.dessertDesc: Spiked tree cake made by dripping egg-rich batter onto a rotating spit over a fire.
LT.drinkDesc: Fermented rye-bread drink, and traditional Lithuanian honey mead.

LU.mainDish1Desc: Smoked pork collar boiled with vegetables and served with broad beans in a cream sauce and potatoes.
LU.mainDish2Desc: Green bean soup with potatoes, onions and bacon or sausage.
LU.streetFoodDesc: Fried patties of grated potato, onion and parsley sold at fairs and Christmas markets.
LU.dessertDesc: Tart of halved damson plums baked on shortcrust or yeast dough, eaten in late summer.
LU.drinkDesc: Sparkling wine and dry white Riesling from the Luxembourg Moselle valley.

MT.mainDish1Desc: Rabbit marinated in wine and garlic, then stewed with tomatoes, peas and bay leaves; the sauce is often served with spaghetti.
MT.mainDish2Desc: Pastry pie of dolphinfish (mahi-mahi) with spinach, olives, capers and tomato, made in autumn.
MT.streetFoodDesc: Flaky diamond-shaped pastries filled with ricotta or mushy peas.
MT.dessertDesc: Diamond-shaped pastries filled with spiced date paste and deep-fried.
MT.drinkDesc: Bitter orange and wormwood soft drink, and Maltese lager.

MC.mainDish1Desc: Fried pastry parcels filled with Swiss chard, ricotta, onion and Parmesan, eaten on Monaco's National Day.
MC.mainDish2Desc: Dried stockfish stewed with tomatoes, black olives, garlic and white wine.
MC.streetFoodDesc: Thin chickpea-flour pancake baked in a wood oven and seasoned with black pepper, shared with nearby Nice.
MC.dessertDesc: Flat orange-blossom-flavoured bread topped with almonds and red and white aniseed sugar.
MC.drinkDesc: Liqueur made from the bitter oranges lining Monaco's streets, and the anise aperitif of the Riviera.

MD.mainDish1Desc: Thick cornmeal porridge served with brânză sheep's cheese and smântână sour cream; shared with Romania.
MD.mainDish2Desc: Sour chicken soup with homemade noodles, vegetables and lovage, soured with borș.
MD.streetFoodDesc: Thin pan-fried or baked pies filled with cheese, potato, cabbage or pumpkin.
MD.dessertDesc: Cone-shaped cake of pastry tubes filled with sour cherries and layered with sour cream.
MD.drinkDesc: Moldovan red and white wines, and Divin, an aged grape brandy.

ME.mainDish1Desc: Mountain dish of cornmeal and potatoes stirred with kajmak and cheese until smooth, shared with neighbouring Balkan countries.
ME.mainDish2Desc: Lamb and potatoes slow-roasted under a metal bell covered with hot coals.
ME.streetFoodDesc: Small fried dough puffs served with honey, cheese or jam.
ME.dessertDesc: Custard slice of puff pastry and vanilla cream, popular across the former Yugoslavia.
ME.drinkDesc: Dry red wine from the native Vranac grape, and grape rakija.

RO.mainDish1Desc: Sour cabbage leaves rolled around minced pork and rice, slow-cooked with smoked meat and served with mămăligă and sour cream.
RO.mainDish2Desc: Sour tripe soup thickened with egg yolk and sour cream, seasoned with garlic and vinegar.
RO.streetFoodDesc: Skinless grilled rolls of minced beef, lamb and pork with garlic and spices, served with mustard.
RO.dessertDesc: Fried cheese doughnuts topped with sour cream and berry jam.
RO.drinkDesc: Plum brandy, and red wine from the native Fetească Neagră grape.

SM.mainDish1Desc: Baked rolls of fresh pasta sheets filled with ham, cheese and béchamel, covered in tomato sauce.
SM.mainDish2Desc: Beans stewed with pork rind, tomato and herbs, a traditional winter and Christmas dish.
SM.streetFoodDesc: Unleavened flatbread cooked on a griddle and folded around cured ham, squacquerone cheese and greens, shared with Romagna.
SM.dessertDesc: Layered wafer cake filled with hazelnut and chocolate cream, named after San Marino's three towers.
SM.drinkDesc: Red and sweet sparkling white wines produced on San Marino's hillside vineyards.

RS.mainDish1Desc: Large grilled patty of spiced minced pork, beef and lamb, served in lepinja flatbread with kajmak, ajvar and onion.
RS.mainDish2Desc: Rolled pork or veal cutlet stuffed with kajmak, breaded and fried, served with tartar sauce.
RS.streetFoodDesc: Layered filo pie baked with eggs and white cheese, sold by bakeries.
RS.dessertDesc: Belgrade cake of ground walnut layers with chocolate and orange cream.
RS.drinkDesc: Plum brandy, inscribed by UNESCO as Serbian intangible heritage in 2022.

SK.mainDish1Desc: Small potato dumplings mixed with soft sheep's cheese (bryndza) and topped with crispy bacon.
SK.mainDish2Desc: Sauerkraut soup with smoked sausage, mushrooms and dried plums, eaten at Christmas.
SK.streetFoodDesc: Thin potato flatbreads baked on a hot plate and filled with goose fat, poppy seeds or jam.
SK.dessertDesc: Crescent pastries filled with ground walnuts or poppy seeds.
SK.drinkDesc: Juniper-berry spirit, and a herbal cola-style soft drink.

SI.mainDish1Desc: Smoked pork sausage seasoned with garlic and pepper, served with mustard, sauerkraut and bread; EU-protected since 2015.
SI.mainDish2Desc: Small hat-shaped dumplings filled with potato, onion and herbs, served with lamb sauce (bakalca).
SI.streetFoodDesc: Filo pastry filled with cheese or meat, sold around the clock in Slovenian towns and shared across the Balkans.
SI.dessertDesc: Rolled yeast cake with a spiral filling, most often ground walnuts, honey or tarragon.
SI.drinkDesc: Light red blend from Dolenjska, and a deep red wine from the Karst plateau.

MK.mainDish1Desc: White beans baked in a clay dish with onions, dried red peppers and paprika.
MK.mainDish2Desc: Trout from Lake Ohrid grilled or baked with garlic, olive oil and lemon.
MK.streetFoodDesc: Boat-shaped dough baked with cubes of cured pork or mutton and often topped with egg, from Štip.
MK.dessertDesc: Fried ridged dough fingers soaked in sugar syrup, an Ottoman-era sweet shared across the Balkans.
MK.drinkDesc: Red wine from the Vranec grape, and an anise-mastic spirit from Strumica.

GG.mainDish1Desc: Haricot and butter beans slow-cooked overnight in an earthenware jar with pork hock or beef shin, onion and herbs.
GG.mainDish2Desc: Ormers (abalone) gathered at low spring tides, tenderised, browned and slowly braised with bacon and onions.
GG.streetFoodDesc: Fruit loaf of yeast dough enriched with Guernsey butter, sultanas and mixed peel, eaten buttered.
GG.dessertDesc: Moist apple cake made with suet, flour and sugar, traditionally baked in the autumn.

JE.mainDish1Desc: Beans slow-cooked in an earthenware crock with pig's trotter or shin of beef and onion, traditionally left in the oven overnight.
JE.mainDish2Desc: Protected-name new potatoes grown on the island's south-facing côtils, boiled and served with Jersey butter.
JE.streetFoodDesc: Rock oysters farmed in the Royal Bay of Grouville, eaten raw with lemon.
JE.dessertDesc: Twisted pieces of sweet dough deep-fried in fat, traditionally cooked as the tide went out.
JE.drinkDesc: Cider from island orchards, and rich milk from the native Jersey cow.

IM.mainDish1Desc: Boiled potatoes in their skins with boiled or salted herring, regarded as the Manx national dish.
IM.mainDish2Desc: Herring split and cold-smoked over oak chips in Peel, grilled and served with bread and butter.
IM.streetFoodDesc: Chips topped with grated cheese and hot gravy, a popular Manx takeaway.
IM.dessertDesc: Traditional Manx soda bread, often made with dried fruit and eaten with butter.
IM.drinkDesc: Beer from the Douglas brewery founded in 1850, brewed under the 1874 Manx Pure Beer Act.

XK.mainDish1Desc: Thin crêpe-like batter layers brushed with cream and baked one at a time under a saç lid covered in embers.
XK.mainDish2Desc: Pie of hand-stretched filo layers filled with minced meat, spinach or cheese.
XK.streetFoodDesc: Small grilled minced-beef sausages served with bread, onions and kajmak.
XK.dessertDesc: Sponge cake soaked in three types of milk and topped with caramel.
XK.drinkDesc: Lager brewed in Peja, and grape or plum rakia.

BA.mainDish1Desc: Small grilled sausages of minced beef served in somun flatbread with chopped onion and kajmak.
BA.mainDish2Desc: Bosnian pot stew of layered meat and vegetables slow-cooked in a clay pot.
BA.streetFoodDesc: Spiral of filo pastry filled only with minced meat; versions with other fillings are called pita.
BA.dessertDesc: Whole apples poached in sugar syrup, stuffed with walnuts and topped with whipped cream.
BA.drinkDesc: Coffee brewed in a copper džezva and served with sugar cubes and rahat lokum, and fruit brandy.

AD.mainDish1Desc: Winter stew of meats, botifarra sausage, a large meatball, chickpeas and vegetables, served first as broth with pasta and then as meat.
AD.mainDish2Desc: Mashed cabbage and potatoes fried as a cake with garlic and pork belly.
AD.streetFoodDesc: Bread rubbed with ripe tomato, olive oil and salt, often topped with cured ham, as across Catalonia.
AD.dessertDesc: Custard flavoured with lemon zest and cinnamon under a caramelised sugar crust, shared with Catalonia.
AD.drinkDesc: Herbal liqueur of green walnuts and spices macerated in spirit.

AL.mainDish1Desc: Baked lamb and rice covered with a thick custard of yogurt and eggs.
AL.mainDish2Desc: Baked dish of peppers, tomatoes and cottage cheese, sometimes with liver or meat.
AL.streetFoodDesc: Filo pie filled with spinach, cheese, meat or onions, sold in slices from bakeries.
AL.dessertDesc: Layers of filo with chopped walnuts soaked in syrup, made for New Year and religious holidays.
AL.drinkDesc: Grape or mulberry brandy, and a salted yogurt drink.

MM.mainDish1Desc: Rice vermicelli in a fish broth thickened with toasted rice and chickpea flour, flavoured with lemongrass, ginger and banana stem, and topped with crispy fritters and boiled egg.
MM.mainDish2Desc: Fermented tea leaves tossed with fried beans, peanuts, sesame, dried shrimp, tomato, cabbage, garlic and lime.
MM.streetFoodDesc: Small round rice-flour batter cakes cooked in a dimpled cast-iron pan with quail egg, chickpeas or spring onion, then paired face to face.
MM.dessertDesc: Chilled coconut milk with agar jelly, sago pearls, soaked sticky rice and slices of white bread.
MM.drinkDesc: Strong black tea sweetened with condensed milk served in teashops, and toddy fermented from the sap of the toddy palm.

KH.mainDish1Desc: Freshwater fish steamed in banana-leaf cups with coconut milk, egg and kroeung paste of lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and kaffir lime.
KH.mainDish2Desc: Stir-fried cubes of marinated beef served on lettuce and tomato with a dipping sauce of lime juice, salt and Kampot pepper.
KH.streetFoodDesc: Thin slices of pork marinated in garlic and coconut milk, grilled over charcoal and served with broken rice and pickled vegetables.
KH.dessertDesc: Glutinous rice wrapped around banana with coconut milk and black beans, bound in banana leaves and steamed.
KH.drinkDesc: Fresh sugarcane juice pressed at street carts, and Angkor, the country's most popular lager.

LK.mainDish1Desc: A plate of rice served with several curries such as dhal, fish or chicken and vegetables, along with pol sambol and papadam.
LK.mainDish2Desc: Bowl-shaped pancakes of fermented rice flour and coconut milk cooked in a small wok, often with an egg cracked into the centre.
LK.streetFoodDesc: Chopped godamba roti stir-fried on a griddle with vegetables, egg, meat and curry sauce.
LK.dessertDesc: Steamed custard pudding of coconut milk, kithul jaggery, eggs, cardamom and nutmeg.
LK.drinkDesc: Black tea grown in the central highlands, and coconut arrack distilled from fermented coconut palm sap.

TW.mainDish1Desc: Wheat noodles in a broth of beef shank braised with soy sauce, chili bean paste and star anise, topped with pickled mustard greens.
TW.mainDish2Desc: Steamed rice topped with minced pork belly braised in soy sauce, rice wine, five-spice and fried shallots.
TW.streetFoodDesc: Small oysters fried with egg and a sweet potato starch batter, finished with a sweet and savoury red sauce.
TW.dessertDesc: Square buttery shortbread pastry filled with cooked pineapple jam.
TW.drinkDesc: Sweetened milk tea with chewy tapioca pearls, and high-mountain oolong tea grown in areas such as Alishan.

GE.mainDish1Desc: Cheese-filled bread made with sulguni and imeruli cheese; the Adjarian version is boat-shaped and topped with egg yolk and butter.
GE.mainDish2Desc: Twisted dumplings filled with spiced minced beef and pork and hot broth, eaten by hand.
GE.streetFoodDesc: Baked bread filled with mashed kidney beans seasoned with onion and spices.
GE.dessertDesc: Strings of walnuts dipped repeatedly in thickened grape juice and dried into chewy candles.
GE.drinkDesc: Dry red wine from the Saperavi grape, often fermented in clay qvevri, and chacha, a brandy distilled from grape pomace.

PS.mainDish1Desc: Taboon flatbread topped with roast chicken, onions slow-cooked in olive oil with plenty of sumac, and toasted pine nuts.
PS.mainDish2Desc: Rice layered with fried eggplant or cauliflower and chicken or lamb, cooked in one pot and flipped upside down to serve.
PS.streetFoodDesc: Oblong ring of sesame bread from Jerusalem, eaten with za'atar, falafel or boiled eggs.
PS.dessertDesc: Nablus dessert of white brined Nabulsi cheese under a layer of semolina or shredded pastry, soaked in sugar syrup.
PS.drinkDesc: Black tea brewed with sage leaves, and Arabic coffee spiced with cardamom.

HK.mainDish1Desc: Small Cantonese dishes such as har gow shrimp dumplings, siu mai and char siu bao, steamed in bamboo baskets and eaten with tea at yum cha.
HK.mainDish2Desc: Thin egg noodles in a shrimp and dried flounder broth with shrimp and pork wontons.
HK.streetFoodDesc: Sweet egg batter cooked in a mould of small spheres, giving a bubble-shaped waffle eaten hot.
HK.dessertDesc: Shortcrust or flaky pastry shells filled with a smooth baked egg custard.
HK.drinkDesc: Strong black tea strained through a cloth filter and mixed with evaporated milk, and yuenyeung, a blend of coffee and milk tea.

IR.mainDish1Desc: Saffron-topped steamed rice served with grilled kabab koobideh of minced lamb or beef, grilled tomatoes, butter and sumac.
IR.mainDish2Desc: Stew of sautéed parsley, coriander, chives and fenugreek cooked with lamb, kidney beans and dried limes.
IR.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of lamb liver, heart and kidney grilled over charcoal and served with flatbread, raw onion and basil.
IR.dessertDesc: Saffron rice pudding flavoured with rosewater and cardamom, decorated with cinnamon and slivered almonds.
IR.drinkDesc: Black tea served with sugar cubes, and doogh, a salted yogurt drink with dried mint.

IQ.mainDish1Desc: Carp split open, seasoned with salt, tamarind and turmeric, and slow-roasted upright beside an open wood fire.
IQ.mainDish2Desc: Onions, peppers, eggplant and grape leaves stuffed with rice and minced meat, cooked in a sour tomato sauce.
IQ.streetFoodDesc: Fried croquettes with a bulgur or rice shell filled with spiced minced meat and onions.
IQ.dessertDesc: Cardamom-scented cookies filled with dates or nuts, traditionally baked for Eid.
IQ.drinkDesc: Strong sweet black tea served in small istikan glasses, and shinina, a salted yogurt drink.

IL.mainDish1Desc: Deep-fried balls of ground chickpeas and herbs served in pita with hummus, tahini, chopped salad and pickles.
IL.mainDish2Desc: Eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, peppers and onions spiced with cumin and paprika.
IL.streetFoodDesc: Pita filled with fried eggplant, hard-boiled egg, tahini, amba mango sauce and chopped salad.
IL.dessertDesc: Milk pudding thickened with starch and topped with rosewater syrup, peanuts and coconut.
IL.drinkDesc: Frozen lemonade blended with fresh mint, and arak, an anise-flavoured grape spirit.

KZ.mainDish1Desc: Boiled horse meat or mutton served over wide sheets of hand-cut noodles with an onion sauce and a bowl of the meat broth.
KZ.mainDish2Desc: Sausage of horse rib meat and fat stuffed into intestine, then dried or smoked and boiled before serving.
KZ.streetFoodDesc: Puffy pieces of fried dough served with tea and at celebrations.
KZ.dessertDesc: Small pieces of fried dough bound together with hot honey syrup into a mound.
KZ.drinkDesc: Kumis is fermented mare's milk and shubat is fermented camel's milk.

JO.mainDish1Desc: Lamb cooked in a sauce of jameed (dried fermented yogurt), served over rice and shrak flatbread with almonds and pine nuts.
JO.mainDish2Desc: Bedouin barbecue of lamb or chicken with vegetables, slow-cooked on racks in a sealed underground pit.
JO.streetFoodDesc: Fried chickpea fritters served in bread with hummus, tahini, tomatoes and pickles.
JO.dessertDesc: White cheese baked under shredded or semolina pastry and soaked in sugar syrup, topped with pistachios.
JO.drinkDesc: Bitter cardamom-spiced Bedouin coffee served in small cups, and lemonade blended with fresh mint.

KP.mainDish1Desc: Cold buckwheat noodles in a chilled beef broth mixed with radish water kimchi, topped with sliced meat, egg and pear.
KP.mainDish2Desc: Warm rice in hot chicken broth topped with shredded chicken, mushrooms and mung bean pancake.
KP.streetFoodDesc: Rice wrapped in sheets of soybean-residue 'artificial meat' and coated in a spicy chili sauce.
KP.dessertDesc: Half-moon rice cakes filled with sesame, beans or chestnut and steamed on pine needles.
KP.drinkDesc: Lager from the Taedonggang Brewery in Pyongyang, and soju distilled from rice or corn.

KW.mainDish1Desc: Basmati rice cooked with chicken or lamb, tomatoes, onions, dried black limes and baharat spice mix.
KW.mainDish2Desc: Fried zubaidi (silver pomfret) served over rice cooked in a spiced fish stock.
KW.streetFoodDesc: Boiled chickpeas seasoned with salt, cumin and lemon, sold in cups.
KW.dessertDesc: Sponge cake flavoured with saffron and cardamom and topped with sesame seeds.
KW.drinkDesc: Light-roasted Arabic coffee with cardamom and saffron served with dates, and laban, a cultured buttermilk drink.

KG.mainDish1Desc: Boiled mutton or horse meat chopped finely and mixed with flat boiled noodles and onions, served with the broth.
KG.mainDish2Desc: Pieces of mutton and offal fried in fat with onions, often served with flatbread.
KG.streetFoodDesc: Tandoor-baked pastry filled with chopped lamb, onion and lamb fat.
KG.dessertDesc: Squares of fried dough piled on the dastorkon table and eaten with jam, butter or tea.
KG.drinkDesc: Kymyz is fermented mare's milk and maksym is a lightly fermented drink made from grains such as barley.

LA.mainDish1Desc: Minced meat or fish salad dressed with lime juice, fish sauce, toasted ground rice, chilies, mint and shallots.
LA.mainDish2Desc: Shredded green papaya pounded in a mortar with chilies, garlic, lime, tomatoes and padaek fermented fish sauce.
LA.streetFoodDesc: Baguette sandwich filled with pâté, cold cuts, pickled vegetables, herbs and chili sauce.
LA.dessertDesc: Sticky rice with coconut milk, sugar and red beans roasted inside a bamboo tube.
LA.drinkDesc: Beerlao is the national rice-based lager and lao-lao is a distilled rice spirit.

LB.mainDish1Desc: Bulgur kneaded with minced lamb and onion, shaped into fried torpedoes, baked in trays or served raw as kibbeh nayyeh.
LB.mainDish2Desc: Salad of finely chopped parsley and mint with bulgur, tomato and onion, dressed with lemon juice and olive oil.
LB.streetFoodDesc: Flatbread baked with a topping of za'atar and olive oil, or with cheese or minced meat.
LB.dessertDesc: Semolina shortbread cookies stuffed with dates, pistachios or walnuts, pressed in wooden moulds.
LB.drinkDesc: Arak is an anise-flavoured grape spirit and jallab is a syrup of grape molasses, dates and rosewater served with pine nuts.

MO.mainDish1Desc: Macanese dish of minced beef or pork fried with soy sauce, onion and diced potatoes, served with rice and a fried egg.
MO.mainDish2Desc: Grilled chicken coated in a spicy sauce of peanuts, coconut, chilies, garlic and paprika.
MO.streetFoodDesc: A marinated, fried bone-in pork chop served in a crusty bread roll.
MO.dessertDesc: Flaky puff pastry shell filled with egg custard and baked until caramelised on top.
MO.drinkDesc: Light Portuguese wine widely served in Macanese restaurants, and Cantonese-style milk tea made with evaporated milk.

MY.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaf, served with sambal, fried anchovies, roasted peanuts, boiled egg and cucumber.
MY.mainDish2Desc: Beef slow-cooked in coconut milk with lemongrass, galangal, chilies and toasted coconut until the sauce is absorbed.
MY.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of marinated chicken or beef grilled over charcoal and served with peanut sauce, cucumber and rice cakes.
MY.dessertDesc: Shaved ice with green rice-flour jelly, coconut milk and gula melaka palm sugar syrup.
MY.drinkDesc: Black tea with condensed milk, poured back and forth between vessels to give it a frothy top.

MV.mainDish1Desc: Clear broth of boiled tuna eaten with rice, lime, chilies and onions.
MV.mainDish2Desc: Shredded smoked tuna mixed with grated coconut, onion and chili, eaten with roshi flatbread for breakfast.
MV.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough balls filled with a mix of smoked tuna, coconut, onion and chili.
MV.dessertDesc: Rice pudding cooked with coconut milk, sugar and cardamom.
MV.drinkDesc: Raa is fresh, sweet sap tapped from the coconut palm, and kurumba is the water of young coconuts.

MN.mainDish1Desc: Steamed dumplings filled with minced mutton or beef, onion and garlic, eaten especially during Tsagaan Sar.
MN.mainDish2Desc: Mutton cooked in a sealed metal container with hot stones, potatoes and carrots.
MN.streetFoodDesc: Flat, deep-fried pastries filled with minced mutton and onion.
MN.dessertDesc: Fried dough biscuits eaten with tea, butter or clotted cream.
MN.drinkDesc: Suutei tsai is salted milk tea and airag is fermented mare's milk.

OM.mainDish1Desc: Lamb or goat rubbed with a spice paste, wrapped in banana or palm leaves and slow-cooked in an underground pit oven for up to two days.
OM.mainDish2Desc: Whole kingfish spit-roasted and served with lemon-flavoured rice.
OM.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of marinated beef or chicken grilled over charcoal.
OM.dessertDesc: Dense gelatinous sweet of sugar, ghee, starch, rosewater, saffron and cardamom, often with nuts.
OM.drinkDesc: Cardamom-spiced Omani coffee served with dates, and laban, a cultured buttermilk drink.

NP.mainDish1Desc: Steamed rice served with lentil soup, vegetable curry (tarkari) and pickles (achar).
NP.mainDish2Desc: Steamed dumplings filled with minced buffalo, chicken or vegetables, served with a tomato and sesame achar.
NP.streetFoodDesc: Spicy mix of puffed rice, potatoes, onions, chilies, lemon and spices tossed to order.
NP.dessertDesc: Sweetened buffalo-milk yogurt set in clay pots, a speciality of Bhaktapur.
NP.drinkDesc: Chiya is milk tea boiled with sugar and spices, and raksi is a distilled millet or rice spirit.

PK.mainDish1Desc: Beef or mutton shank stew slow-cooked overnight with spices and bone marrow, garnished with ginger, chilies and lemon and eaten with naan.
PK.mainDish2Desc: Chicken or mutton cooked in a wok-like karahi with tomatoes, ginger, garlic and green chilies.
PK.streetFoodDesc: Spiced lentil and meat patty dipped in egg and fried, served in a bun with chutney and onions.
PK.dessertDesc: Rice pudding slowly cooked in milk with sugar and cardamom, garnished with nuts.
PK.drinkDesc: Tea leaves boiled in milk with sugar, and Rooh Afza, a rose-flavoured syrup drink served cold.

TL.mainDish1Desc: Spanish mackerel marinated in tamarind, garlic and chili, then grilled or fried.
TL.mainDish2Desc: Stew of corn, mung beans and pumpkin cooked with onion and garlic.
TL.streetFoodDesc: Rice cooked in coconut milk inside small pouches of woven palm leaves.
TL.dessertDesc: Layered coconut and egg cake of Portuguese-Goan origin, baked in layers.
TL.drinkDesc: Arabica coffee grown in the highlands, and tua mutin, palm wine fermented from palm sap.

QA.mainDish1Desc: Basmati rice cooked with lamb or chicken, tomatoes, dried black limes and a spice blend of cardamom, cinnamon and saffron.
QA.mainDish2Desc: Wheat and meat cooked slowly for hours and beaten into a smooth porridge, served with ghee, especially during Ramadan.
QA.streetFoodDesc: Paper-thin crispy bread cooked on a hot plate and filled with egg, cheese or honey.
QA.dessertDesc: Sweetened vermicelli flavoured with saffron, cardamom and rosewater, topped with a thin omelette.
QA.drinkDesc: Strong black tea boiled with evaporated milk, sugar and cardamom, and Arabic coffee served with dates.

SA.mainDish1Desc: Long-grain rice cooked with chicken or lamb, tomatoes, dried limes and baharat, topped with almonds and raisins.
SA.mainDish2Desc: Cracked wheat cooked slowly with meat, onions and yogurt or milk into a thick porridge.
SA.streetFoodDesc: Thin dough folded around minced meat, egg and leeks and pan-fried until crisp.
SA.dessertDesc: Round cookies from Qassim flavoured with cardamom and filled with dates.
SA.drinkDesc: Lightly roasted coffee brewed with cardamom, cloves and saffron and served with dates, and sobia, a chilled Hejazi drink of soaked bread or barley and spices popular in Ramadan.

SG.mainDish1Desc: Poached chicken served with rice cooked in chicken fat and stock with ginger, garlic and pandan, plus chili and ginger sauces.
SG.mainDish2Desc: Mud crab stir-fried in a thick sweet and spicy tomato and chili gravy thickened with egg, eaten with fried mantou buns.
SG.streetFoodDesc: Flat rice noodles stir-fried with dark soy sauce, prawns, cockles, Chinese sausage, egg and bean sprouts.
SG.dessertDesc: Shaved ice topped with coloured syrups and evaporated milk over red beans, sweet corn, grass jelly and attap seeds.
SG.drinkDesc: Kopi is coffee roasted with butter and sugar and served with condensed milk; the Singapore Sling is a gin cocktail created at the Raffles Hotel.

SY.mainDish1Desc: Shells of bulgur and minced lamb stuffed with spiced meat, onions and pine nuts, then fried, baked or grilled.
SY.mainDish2Desc: Lamb cooked in a sauce of yogurt stabilised with starch and egg, served with rice.
SY.streetFoodDesc: Thinly sliced chicken or lamb roasted on a vertical spit and wrapped in thin bread with garlic sauce and pickles.
SY.dessertDesc: Thin, crisp Damascene cookies coated with sesame seeds on one side and pistachios on the other.
SY.drinkDesc: Jallab is a syrup of grape molasses, dates and rosewater served over ice with pine nuts, and Arabic coffee is spiced with cardamom.

TJ.mainDish1Desc: Pieces of flaky fatir bread soaked in a sauce of dissolved qurut (dried salted yogurt), topped with fried onions, tomatoes and herbs, and eaten by hand.
TJ.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked in a cauldron with lamb, carrots, onions and cumin.
TJ.streetFoodDesc: Triangular pastry filled with lamb and onion and baked on the wall of a tandoor oven.
TJ.dessertDesc: Whipped egg whites and sugar flavoured with liquorice root, eaten with bread during Ramadan.
TJ.drinkDesc: Green tea served in small bowls throughout the day.

AE.mainDish1Desc: Wheat and meat cooked slowly for hours and beaten into a smooth porridge, served with ghee, especially during Ramadan and Eid.
AE.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with lamb, chicken or fish, onions, tomatoes, dried limes and baharat spices.
AE.streetFoodDesc: Emirati pancakes flavoured with saffron and cardamom, served with date syrup and cream cheese.
AE.dessertDesc: Small deep-fried dough balls drizzled with date syrup and sprinkled with sesame seeds.
AE.drinkDesc: Arabic coffee spiced with cardamom and saffron and served with dates, and strong milk tea boiled with cardamom.

TM.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked in a cast-iron cauldron with mutton, carrots and onions.
TM.mainDish2Desc: Torn pieces of bread mixed with boiled mutton, onion and tomato, served in the meat broth.
TM.streetFoodDesc: Thin half-moon pastries filled with meat, pumpkin or greens and fried in oil.
TM.dessertDesc: Small pieces of fried dough served with tea.
TM.drinkDesc: Chal is fermented camel's milk, and green tea (gok chay) is drunk throughout the day.

UZ.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked in a kazan with lamb, yellow carrots, onions, cumin and whole garlic heads, sometimes with chickpeas and raisins.
UZ.mainDish2Desc: Hand-pulled noodles served with a stew of lamb, peppers, tomatoes and other vegetables.
UZ.streetFoodDesc: Flaky pastry filled with lamb and onion and baked on the wall of a tandoor oven.
UZ.dessertDesc: Small pillow-shaped hard candies of pulled sugar and flour, served with tea.
UZ.drinkDesc: Green tea served in small bowls (piala) at every meal.

YE.mainDish1Desc: Bubbling meat-broth stew topped with frothy whipped fenugreek (hulba), served in a stone pot and scooped with flatbread.
YE.mainDish2Desc: Rice and lamb or chicken spiced with hawaij and slow-cooked in a pit oven, a Hadhrami speciality.
YE.streetFoodDesc: Layers of spongy lahoh flatbread soaked in spiced yogurt with herbs, garlic and green chili.
YE.dessertDesc: Layered honey bread of buttered dough baked with black seeds and drenched in honey.
YE.drinkDesc: Qishr is a drink of coffee husks brewed with ginger and cardamom, and shai Adeni is spiced milk tea from Aden.

BN.mainDish1Desc: Sticky sago-starch paste twirled on a bamboo chandas fork and dipped in sour cacah sauce made from binjai or tempoyak.
BN.mainDish2Desc: Plain rice with fried chicken and sambal, wrapped in paper as an inexpensive takeaway meal.
BN.streetFoodDesc: Glutinous rice cooked in coconut milk and steamed in a wrapping of leaves.
BN.dessertDesc: Ring-shaped fried cookies of rice flour and brown sugar, made for Hari Raya.
BN.drinkDesc: Black tea with condensed milk, poured between vessels to give it a frothy top.

BT.mainDish1Desc: Stew of fresh or dried chilies cooked with datshi cheese, onions and tomatoes, served with red rice.
BT.mainDish2Desc: Pork, often fatty or dried, stir-fried and stewed with dried red chilies and radish or bok choy.
BT.streetFoodDesc: Steamed dumplings filled with cheese, beef, pork or vegetables, served with chili sauce.
BT.dessertDesc: Crisp fried biscuits of wheat flour dough twisted into shapes, made for festivals.
BT.drinkDesc: Suja is tea churned with butter and salt, and ara is a home-distilled spirit of rice, millet or maize.

BD.mainDish1Desc: Hilsa fish cooked in a sauce of ground mustard seeds, mustard oil, green chilies and turmeric, eaten with rice.
BD.mainDish2Desc: Dhaka-style biryani of marinated raw mutton layered with rice and potatoes and slow-cooked sealed in a pot.
BD.streetFoodDesc: Crisp hollow shells filled with spiced mashed potato and chickpeas and dipped in tangy tamarind water.
BD.dessertDesc: Sweetened yogurt fermented in clay pots, associated with Bogura.
BD.drinkDesc: Borhani is a spiced yogurt drink with mint and green chili served with biryani, and cha is sweet milk tea.

BH.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked with chicken, lamb or fish, tomatoes, dried limes and a Bahraini spice mix.
BH.mainDish2Desc: Sweet rice cooked with date syrup or sugar, saffron and cardamom, traditionally served with grilled or fried fish.
BH.streetFoodDesc: Thin triangular pastries filled with spiced meat, cheese or vegetables and deep-fried.
BH.dessertDesc: Bahraini halwa of cornstarch, sugar, ghee, saffron and rosewater studded with nuts.
BH.drinkDesc: Arabic coffee spiced with cardamom and served with dates, and laban, a cultured buttermilk drink.

AZ.mainDish1Desc: Saffron rice baked inside a crust of lavash with lamb, chestnuts, dried apricots and raisins.
AZ.mainDish2Desc: Grape leaves, cabbage or vegetables stuffed with minced lamb, rice and herbs, served with garlic yogurt.
AZ.streetFoodDesc: Thin half-moon flatbreads filled with herbs, pumpkin or minced meat and cooked on a griddle.
AZ.dessertDesc: Diamond-shaped layered pastry filled with ground walnuts and spices, soaked in honey syrup and decorated with saffron.
AZ.drinkDesc: Black tea served in pear-shaped armudu glasses with jam, and sherbet, a sweet chilled drink of fruit, rosewater and basil seeds.

AM.mainDish1Desc: Barbecue of pork or lamb marinated with onions and skewered over hot coals, served with grilled vegetables and lavash.
AM.mainDish2Desc: Grape leaves or vegetables stuffed with minced meat, rice and herbs, served with garlic yogurt.
AM.streetFoodDesc: Thin round flatbread baked with a topping of minced meat, tomato, peppers and herbs.
AM.dessertDesc: Sweet pastry bread filled with khoriz, a crumbly mixture of flour, butter and sugar.
AM.drinkDesc: Brandy distilled and aged in Yerevan, and tan, a salted yogurt drink diluted with water.

AF.mainDish1Desc: Rice steamed with lamb broth and topped with tender lamb, caramelised carrots, raisins and almonds.
AF.mainDish2Desc: Steamed dumplings filled with spiced minced beef or lamb and onion, topped with yogurt and a lentil or tomato sauce.
AF.streetFoodDesc: Thin flatbread stuffed with potato, leeks or pumpkin and fried, served with yogurt dip.
AF.dessertDesc: Milk pudding thickened with cornstarch and flavoured with cardamom and rosewater, topped with pistachios.
AF.drinkDesc: Green tea often flavoured with cardamom, and doogh, a salted yogurt drink with mint.

IN.mainDish1Desc: Basmati rice layered with marinated meat or vegetables, saffron, fried onions and whole spices, then cooked sealed (dum).
IN.mainDish2Desc: Crisp fermented rice and lentil crêpe filled with spiced potato, served with sambar and coconut chutney.
IN.streetFoodDesc: Hollow fried puris filled with potato, chickpeas and spiced tamarind and mint water.
IN.dessertDesc: Fried balls of milk solids soaked in a sugar syrup flavoured with cardamom and rosewater.
IN.drinkDesc: Black tea boiled with milk, sugar, ginger and cardamom, and lassi, a blended yogurt drink served sweet or salted.

BI.mainDish1Desc: Red kidney beans boiled until tender, then fried with onions, garlic and palm oil, usually eaten with plantains, cassava paste or rice.
BI.mainDish2Desc: Pounded cassava leaves stewed with palm oil, onions, eggplant and sometimes dried fish or peanut paste.
BI.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of goat or beef grilled over charcoal and served with grilled plantain or chips in bars across Bujumbura.
BI.dessertDesc: Lightly sweetened fried dough buns eaten as a snack with tea.
BI.drinkDesc: Urwarwa is a traditional fermented banana beer shared at ceremonies, and Primus is the most widely drunk bottled lager.

CM.mainDish1Desc: Stew of washed bitterleaf simmered with ground peanuts, beef or shrimp and onions, served with boiled plantains, miondo or bobolo.
CM.mainDish2Desc: Finely shredded eru (okazi) leaves cooked with waterleaf, palm oil, crayfish, smoked fish and cow skin, eaten with water fufu.
CM.streetFoodDesc: Thin strips of beef rubbed with a spicy peanut and pepper mix and grilled on skewers over charcoal.
CM.dessertDesc: Sweet fried dough balls sold by roadside vendors, often eaten with beans (beignets-haricots).
CM.drinkDesc: Matango is fresh palm wine tapped from raffia or oil palms, and foléré is a chilled sweetened hibiscus drink.

CV.mainDish1Desc: Slow-cooked stew of hominy corn and beans with vegetables and fish or meat such as pork, chouriço and chicken; leftovers are fried for breakfast as cachupa guisada.
CV.mainDish2Desc: Fish stew of tuna or wahoo cooked with tomatoes, onions, potatoes, cassava, sweet potato and green banana.
CV.streetFoodDesc: Fried pastries made from corn flour and sweet potato dough filled with spicy tuna.
CV.dessertDesc: Papaya cooked down with sugar into a thick preserve, traditionally served with fresh goat cheese.
CV.drinkDesc: Grogue is a sugarcane spirit distilled mainly on Santo Antão and Santiago, and ponche is a sweet liqueur of grogue mixed with molasses or honey.

CF.mainDish1Desc: Pounded cassava leaves cooked with palm oil or peanut paste and smoked fish or meat, eaten with gozo (cassava paste).
CF.mainDish2Desc: Finely sliced Gnetum (koko) leaves stewed with peanut paste, palm oil and smoked fish or meat.
CF.streetFoodDesc: Edible caterpillars collected in the rainy season, sold dried or fried with onions, tomatoes and pepper.
CF.dessertDesc: Small fried balls of sweetened wheat or cassava dough sold in markets and eaten for breakfast or as a snack.
CF.drinkDesc: Fresh palm wine tapped from oil palms, and Mocaf, the lager brewed in Bangui.

TD.mainDish1Desc: Stiff dough of millet or sorghum flour shaped into a ball and eaten by hand with a sauce such as okra, dried fish or meat stew.
TD.mainDish2Desc: Okra stew cooked with tomatoes, eggplant, greens and peanut butter, served with boule.
TD.streetFoodDesc: Thin fermented sorghum or millet crêpes, sold stacked and eaten with meat or vegetable sauces.
TD.dessertDesc: Fried dough balls of wheat flour, sugar and yeast sold by street vendors in the morning.
TD.drinkDesc: Chilled infusion of dried hibiscus flowers sweetened with sugar and often spiced with ginger or cloves.

KM.mainDish1Desc: Spiny lobster cooked in a creamy sauce flavoured with locally grown vanilla, served with rice.
KM.mainDish2Desc: Pounded cassava leaves slow-cooked in coconut milk, often with fish or meat, and served with rice or boiled plantain.
KM.streetFoodDesc: Triangular fried pastries filled with spiced minced meat or fish.
KM.dessertDesc: Slightly sweet flatbread made with rice or wheat flour and coconut milk, sprinkled with sesame and cooked on a griddle.
KM.drinkDesc: Black tea infused with Comorian vanilla, and coconut water drunk straight from green coconuts.

CG.mainDish1Desc: Pounded cassava leaves simmered for hours with palm oil, onions, peanut paste and smoked or salted fish.
CG.mainDish2Desc: River fish seasoned with chilli, onion and tomato, wrapped in large leaves and cooked over embers or steamed.
CG.streetFoodDesc: Fermented cassava paste steamed in leaves into dense loaves, sold by street vendors to eat with grilled fish or meat.
CG.dessertDesc: Sweet fried dough balls of wheat flour, sugar and yeast, eaten for breakfast or as a snack.
CG.drinkDesc: Fresh palm wine (malafu) tapped from palms, and Ngok', the lager brewed in Brazzaville.

CD.mainDish1Desc: Chicken stewed in a sauce of palm nut pulp with onions, garlic and chilli, served with rice, fufu or kwanga.
CD.mainDish2Desc: Cassava leaves pounded and cooked with palm oil, onions, garlic and dried or smoked fish, eaten with fufu.
CD.streetFoodDesc: Fermented cassava bread steamed in leaves, sold by street vendors with grilled fish or makayabu (salted fish).
CD.dessertDesc: Fried balls of sweetened yeast dough sold in Kinshasa markets as a breakfast snack.
CD.drinkDesc: Primus is the best-known Congolese lager, and malafu is palm wine tapped from oil or raffia palms.

BJ.mainDish1Desc: Red cornmeal paste cooked in a tomato, onion and chicken broth, usually served with fried or stewed chicken.
BJ.mainDish2Desc: Stew of gboma spinach cooked with tomatoes, onions, palm oil and smoked fish or meat, eaten with corn paste (pâte).
BJ.streetFoodDesc: Crunchy rings or sticks of pressed peanut paste fried in peanut oil after the oil has been extracted.
BJ.dessertDesc: Sweet fried dough balls made from wheat flour, sugar and yeast, sold by street vendors.
BJ.drinkDesc: Tchoukoutou is a fermented sorghum beer from the north, and sodabi is a spirit distilled from palm wine.

GQ.mainDish1Desc: Spicy pepper soup of fish or chicken cooked with hot chillies, onions, tomatoes and local herbs.
GQ.mainDish2Desc: Ground pumpkin seeds mixed with fish or meat and spices, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed, a dish of the Fang people.
GQ.streetFoodDesc: Ripe plantain slices fried in oil and sold alongside grilled fish or meat.
GQ.dessertDesc: Small fried dough balls dusted with sugar and sold as a sweet snack.
GQ.drinkDesc: Malamba is an alcoholic drink fermented from sugarcane juice, and osang is a locally drunk African tea.

ER.mainDish1Desc: Spicy stew of beef, lamb or chicken slow-cooked with onions, tomato and berbere, eaten with injera or taita.
ER.mainDish2Desc: Thick stew of ground chickpea or broad bean flour cooked with onions, garlic, oil and berbere, served with injera.
ER.streetFoodDesc: Mashed fava beans topped with onion, tomato, chilli, oil and yogurt, eaten with bread for breakfast.
ER.dessertDesc: Slightly sweet celebration bread flavoured with cardamom or fennel seed, scored in a wheel pattern before baking.
ER.drinkDesc: Coffee roasted and brewed in a jebena during the coffee ceremony, and suwa, a home-brewed barley or millet beer.

DJ.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked with lamb or goat, tomatoes, onions and spices such as cardamom, cumin and cinnamon.
DJ.mainDish2Desc: Spicy soup of boiled goat meat with vegetables, chillies and coriander, eaten with canjeero flatbread.
DJ.streetFoodDesc: Triangular fried pastries filled with spiced minced meat, onions and herbs.
DJ.dessertDesc: Dense, glossy sweet made from sugar, cornstarch, ghee and cardamom, served at weddings and Eid.
DJ.drinkDesc: Black tea brewed with milk, sugar and spices such as cardamom, cinnamon and cloves.

GA.mainDish1Desc: Chicken simmered in a sauce made from palm nut pulp with onions, garlic and chilli, served with rice or plantains.
GA.mainDish2Desc: Sauce made from roasted, ground wild mango (bush mango) kernels, served with smoked fish or meat and cassava.
GA.streetFoodDesc: Safou fruit (bush butter) softened in hot water or on embers and sold at roadsides with cassava sticks.
GA.dessertDesc: Sweet fried dough balls of wheat flour, sugar and yeast, eaten at breakfast or as a snack.
GA.drinkDesc: Régab is the most popular Gabonese lager, and malamba is a fermented sugarcane drink.

GM.mainDish1Desc: Peanut butter stew of beef, chicken or fish with tomatoes, onions and pumpkin or sweet potato, served over rice.
GM.mainDish2Desc: One-pot rice cooked in a tomato and onion sauce with fish or meat and vegetables, related to jollof rice.
GM.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried fritters of mashed black-eyed peas with onion and pepper, often served in bread with a spicy sauce.
GM.dessertDesc: Sweet millet couscous mixed with yogurt or sour milk, sugar, vanilla and nutmeg.
GM.drinkDesc: Wonjo is a chilled sweetened hibiscus drink, and attaya is strong green tea with mint and sugar poured in several rounds.

GH.mainDish1Desc: Boiled cassava and plantain pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, served in light soup, groundnut soup or palm nut soup.
GH.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked in a seasoned tomato, onion and pepper stew, usually served with chicken, beef or fried fish.
GH.streetFoodDesc: Cubes of ripe plantain seasoned with ginger, chilli and spices, then deep-fried.
GH.dessertDesc: Sweet fried dough balls, also called puff-puff, sold by street vendors.
GH.drinkDesc: Sobolo is a chilled hibiscus drink spiced with ginger and cloves, and palm wine is tapped fresh from oil palms.

GN.mainDish1Desc: Finely pounded cassava or sweet potato leaves cooked with palm oil, meat or smoked fish and chilli, served over rice.
GN.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked in a tomato and onion sauce with meat or fish and vegetables such as carrots, cabbage and eggplant.
GN.streetFoodDesc: Fried pastries filled with spiced fish or minced meat, served with a tomato and onion sauce.
GN.dessertDesc: Small grains of millet couscous mixed with sweetened yogurt or curdled milk.
GN.drinkDesc: Bissap is a chilled hibiscus drink, and gnamakoudji is a sweetened fresh ginger juice.

CI.mainDish1Desc: Fermented, grated cassava steamed into a couscous-like grain, typically served with grilled fish, onions, tomatoes and chilli.
CI.mainDish2Desc: Chicken slow-cooked with onions, tomatoes, chilli and ginger in a sealed canari pot without added water.
CI.streetFoodDesc: Ripe plantain slices fried in palm oil and served with chilli and onion sauce, often with grilled fish or boiled eggs.
CI.dessertDesc: Millet couscous mixed with sweetened yogurt or curdled milk and served chilled.
CI.drinkDesc: Bandji is palm wine tapped from oil or raffia palms, and gnamakoudji is a sweetened fresh ginger juice.

KE.mainDish1Desc: Stiff porridge of white maize flour cooked in water, eaten by hand with sukuma wiki, stews or nyama choma.
KE.mainDish2Desc: Goat or beef roasted slowly over charcoal, served with kachumbari salad and ugali.
KE.streetFoodDesc: Sausage of goat or beef intestines stuffed with minced meat, blood and spices, grilled over charcoal.
KE.dessertDesc: Lightly sweet fried dough triangles flavoured with coconut milk or cardamom, eaten with tea.
KE.drinkDesc: Kenyan black tea boiled with milk and sugar, and Tusker, the country's best-known lager.

LS.mainDish1Desc: Stiff maize meal porridge eaten with moroho (cooked greens such as spinach or cabbage) and meat stew.
LS.mainDish2Desc: Dried maize kernels or sorghum boiled together with beans until soft.
LS.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried bread dough balls, also known as fat cakes, sold at taxi ranks and markets.
LS.dessertDesc: Baked sponge pudding made with apricot jam and soaked in a hot butter and cream sauce.
LS.drinkDesc: Joala is a home-brewed sorghum beer, and Maluti is the lager brewed in Maseru.

LR.mainDish1Desc: Thick stew made from palm nut pulp cooked with meat or fish and hot peppers, served over rice.
LR.mainDish2Desc: Pounded cassava leaves stewed with palm oil, chicken or fish, dried fish and hot peppers, eaten over rice.
LR.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough balls sold by street vendors, sometimes made with mashed bananas.
LR.dessertDesc: Moist sweet bread made from cream of rice or rice flour, mashed bananas, sugar and nutmeg.
LR.drinkDesc: Homemade non-alcoholic ginger beer made from fresh ginger and sugar, and palm wine tapped from oil palms.

LY.mainDish1Desc: Dome of stiff barley flour dough set in a spicy tomato sauce with lamb, potatoes and hard-boiled eggs, eaten by hand.
LY.mainDish2Desc: Lamb soup with tomato, chickpeas, orzo-shaped pasta, mint and spices, served especially during Ramadan.
LY.streetFoodDesc: Fried rings of yeast dough, eaten plain with sugar or honey or with a fried egg cooked into the centre.
LY.dessertDesc: Thick wheat flour dough served with rub (date syrup) and melted butter or olive oil.
LY.drinkDesc: Strong black tea poured from a height to raise a foam, often served with mint or roasted peanuts.

MG.mainDish1Desc: Broth of zebu beef cooked with brèdes mafana (paracress) and other leafy greens, ginger and tomato, served with rice.
MG.mainDish2Desc: Pounded cassava leaves cooked slowly with pork and garlic, eaten with rice.
MG.streetFoodDesc: Slightly sweet rice-flour cakes cooked in round cast-iron moulds and sold at breakfast stalls.
MG.dessertDesc: Paste of ground peanuts, rice flour, banana and sugar wrapped in banana leaves and boiled for hours, then sold in slices.
MG.drinkDesc: Ranovola is water boiled in the pot with toasted rice, and THB (Three Horses Beer) is the national lager.

MW.mainDish1Desc: Stiff porridge of maize flour shaped into patties and eaten by hand with relishes of greens, beans, fish or meat.
MW.mainDish2Desc: Tilapia from Lake Malawi grilled or fried whole and served with nsima and tomato relish.
MW.streetFoodDesc: Fried sweet dough buns sold at roadsides and eaten with tea.
MW.dessertDesc: Fritters made from mashed ripe bananas, maize flour and sugar.
MW.drinkDesc: Thick, lightly fermented non-alcoholic drink made from maize or millet flour and sugar.

ML.mainDish1Desc: Stew of beef or lamb cooked in a peanut butter and tomato sauce with onions and vegetables, served over rice.
ML.mainDish2Desc: Thick paste of millet or sorghum flour eaten with a sauce of okra or baobab leaves.
ML.streetFoodDesc: Millet porridge with small dumplings, flavoured with tamarind or lemon and sugar, sold for breakfast.
ML.dessertDesc: Millet couscous mixed with sweetened yogurt or curdled milk.
ML.drinkDesc: Bissap is a chilled hibiscus drink, and gnamakoudji is sweetened fresh ginger juice.

MR.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked in a tomato sauce with fish and vegetables such as cabbage, cassava, carrots and eggplant.
MR.mainDish2Desc: Whole lamb roasted slowly over coals, served at celebrations and for honoured guests.
MR.streetFoodDesc: Fried pastries filled with spiced fish or minced meat.
MR.dessertDesc: Millet couscous mixed with sweetened curdled milk or yogurt.
MR.drinkDesc: Atay is green tea with mint and sugar served in three rounds, and zrig is sweetened camel or goat milk mixed with water.

MU.mainDish1Desc: Thin flatbread stuffed with ground yellow split peas, served with bean curry, rougaille and chutneys.
MU.mainDish2Desc: Tomato-based sauce with onions, garlic, ginger, thyme and chilli, cooked with sausages, salted fish or seafood and served with rice.
MU.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried balls of ground split peas with chilli, spring onion and coriander.
MU.dessertDesc: Two shortbread rounds sandwiched with jam and covered in pink icing.
MU.drinkDesc: Alouda is a cold milk drink with basil seeds, agar jelly and vanilla or rose syrup, and Mauritian rum is distilled from sugarcane.

MZ.mainDish1Desc: Pounded cassava leaves cooked with ground peanuts, coconut milk and garlic, often with crab or prawns, served with rice.
MZ.mainDish2Desc: Chicken marinated in coconut milk, lime, garlic and chilli, then grilled and served with coconut sauce.
MZ.streetFoodDesc: Triangular fried pastries filled with spiced minced meat, fish or vegetables.
MZ.dessertDesc: Dense cake made with ground cashew nuts and mashed potato, butter, sugar and eggs.
MZ.drinkDesc: 2M is the national lager, and Tipo Tinto is a local rum commonly mixed with raspberry soda.

NA.mainDish1Desc: Stiff porridge of mahangu (pearl millet) flour eaten by hand with meat stew, spinach or dried mopane worms.
NA.mainDish2Desc: Meat and vegetables slow-cooked in layers in a three-legged cast-iron pot over coals.
NA.streetFoodDesc: Small pieces of beef grilled on open fires at markets and dipped in a spicy salt and chilli mix.
NA.dessertDesc: Braided fried dough soaked in cold sugar syrup.
NA.drinkDesc: Oshikundu is a lightly fermented drink of mahangu and sorghum malt, and Windhoek Lager is brewed under the German Reinheitsgebot.

NE.mainDish1Desc: A stiff paste of millet or sorghum flour served with a thick sauce of dried, powdered baobab leaves, dried okra and spices, sometimes with meat.
NE.mainDish2Desc: Steamed couscous of millet, maize or rice grits mixed with moringa leaves, onions and groundnut, often served with a meat or tomato sauce.
NE.streetFoodDesc: Thin sheets of beef dried in the sun and coated with a paste of ground peanuts, chilli and spices before a final roasting.
NE.dessertDesc: Balls of spiced millet dough crumbled into fermented milk and sweetened with sugar.
NE.drinkDesc: Chilled sweetened hibiscus infusion, and strong green tea with mint served in three successive rounds.

GW.mainDish1Desc: A stew of fish or chicken cooked in a sauce made from pounded palm nut pulp with onion and chilli, served over white rice.
GW.mainDish2Desc: A peanut-based stew of chicken or fish with tomato, onion and chilli, eaten with rice.
GW.streetFoodDesc: Mangrove oysters grilled over charcoal and served with a lime and chilli sauce, sold around Bissau.
GW.dessertDesc: A sweet of grated coconut cooked with sugar until thick and sticky.
GW.drinkDesc: Fermented juice of the cashew apple, a by-product of the country's main cash crop, and sweet hibiscus juice.

RW.mainDish1Desc: Pounded cassava leaves stewed with eggplant, spinach, onions and peanut paste or palm oil.
RW.mainDish2Desc: Green cooking bananas stewed with tomato, onion and sometimes meat or beans.
RW.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of goat meat grilled over charcoal and served with grilled plantain or fries.
RW.dessertDesc: Lightly sweet fried dough triangles, often flavoured with cardamom, eaten with tea.
RW.drinkDesc: Thick fermented milk, and a traditional beer brewed from ripe bananas and sorghum.

SH.mainDish1Desc: A pilau-style rice dish cooked with curry spices, onions and meat such as chicken, pork or tuna, sometimes with bacon.
SH.mainDish2Desc: Patties of minced local tuna mixed with mashed potato, onion, herbs and chilli, then fried.
SH.streetFoodDesc: Small fried fritters of mashed pumpkin and flour, served dusted with sugar.
SH.dessertDesc: Sponge fingers coated in jam or icing and rolled in desiccated coconut.
SH.drinkDesc: Coffee grown on the island from Green Tipped Bourbon Arabica plants, and Tungi, a spirit distilled from the fruit of the prickly pear cactus.

ST.mainDish1Desc: A slow-cooked stew of smoked fish or chicken with okra, eggplant, tomatoes and a mix of local herbs and leaves in palm oil, served with funge or rice.
ST.mainDish2Desc: Seeds of the African breadfruit simmered with palm oil, fish and greens.
ST.streetFoodDesc: The purple fruit of the safou tree, briefly boiled or roasted and eaten as a snack.
ST.dessertDesc: A chewy sweet of grated coconut cooked with sugar.
ST.drinkDesc: Palm wine tapped from oil palms and drunk fresh and lightly fermented.

SN.mainDish1Desc: Broken rice cooked in a tomato broth with fish stuffed with parsley, garlic and chilli, plus cassava, cabbage, carrots and eggplant.
SN.mainDish2Desc: Chicken marinated in lemon juice, mustard and large amounts of onion, then grilled and simmered in the caramelised onion sauce, served with rice.
SN.streetFoodDesc: Lamb grilled over charcoal and served with raw onion, mustard and bread.
SN.dessertDesc: Millet couscous mixed with sweetened yogurt or curdled milk, often flavoured with nutmeg and vanilla.
SN.drinkDesc: Sweet hibiscus drink, and coffee roasted with grains of Selim pepper and cloves.

SC.mainDish1Desc: A Creole curry of octopus or fish cooked in coconut milk with garlic, ginger, turmeric and curry spices, served with rice.
SC.mainDish2Desc: Boiled shark meat, finely mashed and fried with bilimbi, lime juice, onion, garlic and chilli.
SC.streetFoodDesc: Triangular fried pastries filled with spiced fish, chicken or vegetables sold at takeaways.
SC.dessertDesc: Ripe plantain or breadfruit simmered in coconut milk with sugar, nutmeg and vanilla.
SC.drinkDesc: Lemongrass tea grown and brewed locally, and the locally brewed SeyBrew lager.

SL.mainDish1Desc: Pounded cassava leaves stewed in palm oil with fish, meat or chicken, onions and chilli, served over rice.
SL.mainDish2Desc: A thick peanut-based stew of chicken or beef with tomato, onion and chilli, eaten with rice.
SL.streetFoodDesc: Small fritters of rice flour, mashed ripe banana and sugar, deep-fried and sold on the street.
SL.dessertDesc: A sweet bar of ground roasted peanuts, toasted rice flour or gari and sugar pressed together.
SL.drinkDesc: Homemade non-alcoholic drink of grated fresh ginger, sugar and lime, served cold.

SO.mainDish1Desc: Basmati rice cooked with xawaash spice mix, onion, tomato and goat or lamb, often topped with raisins and served with a banana on the side.
SO.mainDish2Desc: Small cubes of beef, goat or camel meat sautéed with onions, peppers and spices, eaten with canjeero flatbread, rice or pasta.
SO.streetFoodDesc: Fried triangular pastries filled with spiced minced meat or tuna, onion and green chilli.
SO.dessertDesc: A dense, glossy confection of sugar, cornstarch, ghee, cardamom and nutmeg, served at weddings and Eid.
SO.drinkDesc: Sweet black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, and fresh camel milk.

ZA.mainDish1Desc: Curried minced meat baked with dried fruit and chutney under an egg-and-milk topping, served with yellow rice.
ZA.mainDish2Desc: Meat such as boerewors sausage, lamb chops and steak grilled over wood or charcoal, usually served with pap and chakalaka.
ZA.streetFoodDesc: A hollowed-out loaf of white bread filled with mutton, chicken or bean curry, from Durban.
ZA.dessertDesc: A spongy baked pudding containing apricot jam, soaked in a hot butter and cream sauce.
ZA.drinkDesc: Caffeine-free red bush tea from the Cederberg, and Pinotage, a red wine grape bred in South Africa.

ZW.mainDish1Desc: A stiff porridge of finely ground white maize eaten by hand with a relish of stewed beef or chicken and leafy greens.
ZW.mainDish2Desc: Leafy greens such as covo or pumpkin leaves cooked with tomato, onion and peanut butter.
ZW.streetFoodDesc: Mopane worms, dried and then fried or stewed with tomato and onion, eaten as a protein-rich snack.
ZW.dessertDesc: Strips of green papaya boiled in sugar syrup until candied.
ZW.drinkDesc: A thick, slightly sour fermented maize drink, and a commercially brewed opaque sorghum beer.

SS.mainDish1Desc: A thin fermented sorghum flatbread cooked on a griddle and eaten with stews of okra, meat or dried fish.
SS.mainDish2Desc: A thick sorghum or maize porridge served with a stew of meat, okra or peanut sauce.
SS.streetFoodDesc: Fried triangular pastries filled with spiced minced meat or lentils.
SS.dessertDesc: Fried, lightly sweetened dough pieces commonly eaten with tea.
SS.drinkDesc: Sweet black tea, and a home-brewed sorghum beer.

SD.mainDish1Desc: Slow-cooked fava beans mashed with oil, cumin and salt, often topped with feta, onion, tomato and egg and eaten with bread.
SD.mainDish2Desc: Thin fermented sorghum flatbread served with a stew such as weika, made from dried okra and meat.
SD.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried patties of ground chickpeas or fava beans with herbs and spices, usually eaten in bread.
SD.dessertDesc: A semolina cake baked with yogurt and coconut and soaked in sugar syrup.
SD.drinkDesc: Hibiscus infusion served cold or hot, and coffee brewed with ginger in a clay jabana pot.

EH.mainDish1Desc: Steamed semolina or barley grains topped with a stew of camel, goat or lamb and vegetables.
EH.mainDish2Desc: A whole lamb or goat roasted slowly over embers or in a pit until the meat pulls from the bone.
EH.streetFoodDesc: Square, flaky pan-fried flatbread made from folded semolina dough, eaten with honey or butter.
EH.dessertDesc: Flower-shaped fried dough with sesame and anise, soaked in honey and eaten especially during Ramadan.
EH.drinkDesc: Strong sweet green tea poured from height in three rounds, and zrig, a sweetened drink of milk or curdled milk diluted with water.

SZ.mainDish1Desc: A thick porridge of maize meal served with stewed meat, usually beef or chicken, or vegetables.
SZ.mainDish2Desc: A porridge of pumpkin cooked with maize meal and sometimes milk.
SZ.streetFoodDesc: Salted and spiced strips of beef dried in the air, similar to biltong.
SZ.dessertDesc: Deep-fried balls of slightly sweet yeast dough sold by roadside vendors.
SZ.drinkDesc: A fermented maize drink, and buganu, a beer brewed from marula fruit and celebrated at the Marula Festival.

TG.mainDish1Desc: Boiled yam pounded into a smooth, elastic dough and served with a peanut, palm nut or tomato soup with meat or fish.
TG.mainDish2Desc: A spinach stew with tomatoes, onions, palm oil and smoked fish or meat, served with akoumé maize dough.
TG.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried strips of yam served with a chilli sauce.
TG.dessertDesc: Fried balls of sweetened yeast dough, similar to puff-puff.
TG.drinkDesc: A fermented sorghum beer from the north, and sodabi, a spirit distilled from palm wine.

TN.mainDish1Desc: Steamed semolina served with a spicy harissa-red sauce of lamb, fish or chicken with chickpeas, carrots, pumpkin and peppers.
TN.mainDish2Desc: Eggs poached in a spicy tomato and pepper sauce with harissa and garlic, often with merguez or seafood.
TN.streetFoodDesc: A crisp fried pastry of thin malsouka dough filled with a whole egg, tuna, capers and parsley.
TN.dessertDesc: Diamond-shaped semolina pastries filled with date paste, fried or baked and dipped in honey syrup.
TN.drinkDesc: Sweet green tea with fresh mint, served with pine nuts floating in the glass.

UG.mainDish1Desc: Green cooking bananas peeled, steamed in banana leaves and mashed, served with groundnut sauce, beans or meat stew.
UG.mainDish2Desc: Chicken, beef or fish stewed with groundnut paste or vegetables, wrapped and steamed in banana leaves.
UG.streetFoodDesc: An omelette with cabbage, tomato and onion rolled up in a chapati.
UG.dessertDesc: Fried, lightly sweetened dough pieces commonly eaten with tea.
UG.drinkDesc: A distilled spirit traditionally made from bananas or millet, and a fermented sorghum or millet drink from western Uganda.

TZ.mainDish1Desc: A stiff white maize-flour porridge eaten by hand with fish, meat stew or sautéed greens.
TZ.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked in broth with meat, onions, garlic and whole spices such as cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves.
TZ.streetFoodDesc: French fries cooked into an omelette, served with ketchup and kachumbari salad.
TZ.dessertDesc: Small round fried cakes of rice flour, coconut milk, sugar and cardamom.
TZ.drinkDesc: Spiced milky tea, and strong black coffee sold in small cups by street vendors in Zanzibar and the coast.

BF.mainDish1Desc: A thick paste of millet, sorghum or maize flour served with a sauce of okra, baobab leaves or sorrel.
BF.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked in a tomato and onion sauce with meat and vegetables.
BF.streetFoodDesc: Lean free-range chicken grilled or roasted whole and sold by street vendors.
BF.dessertDesc: Small grains of millet couscous mixed with sweetened yogurt or curdled milk.
BF.drinkDesc: A cold drink of millet flour, ginger, lemon and tamarind, and dolo, a home-brewed sorghum beer.

ZM.mainDish1Desc: A stiff white maize porridge eaten by hand with relishes such as stewed beef, chicken, kapenta fish or greens.
ZM.mainDish2Desc: Greens such as pumpkin leaves or spinach cooked in a sauce of ground peanuts, tomato and onion.
ZM.streetFoodDesc: A savoury loaf of ground orchid tubers, peanuts and chilli, sliced and eaten as a snack.
ZM.dessertDesc: Fried balls of sweetened dough sold at markets and roadsides.
ZM.drinkDesc: A lightly fermented maize drink flavoured with munkoyo root, and Mosi, the national lager.

BW.mainDish1Desc: Beef or goat boiled with salt until tender and then pounded into shreds, served with bogobe or pap.
BW.mainDish2Desc: A thick porridge of sorghum or maize meal, sometimes cooked with melon (lerotse) or sour milk.
BW.streetFoodDesc: Mopane worms, dried and then fried or stewed with tomato and onion.
BW.dessertDesc: Deep-fried balls of slightly sweet yeast dough, also known as fat cakes.
BW.drinkDesc: A thick fermented maize drink, and a commercially brewed opaque sorghum beer.

IO.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaf, served with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.
IO.mainDish2Desc: Rice noodles in a spicy coconut curry broth with prawns, tofu puffs and bean sprouts.
IO.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of marinated chicken or beef grilled over charcoal and served with peanut sauce.
IO.dessertDesc: Small steamed or baked cakes made from rice flour, coconut and palm sugar.
IO.drinkDesc: Strong black tea with condensed milk, poured back and forth between vessels to make it frothy.

AO.mainDish1Desc: Chicken stewed in palm oil with okra, garlic, onion and chilli, served with funge cassava porridge.
AO.mainDish2Desc: Grilled whole fish served with beans cooked in palm oil, boiled sweet potato, plantain and cassava, and a raw onion and vinegar sauce.
AO.streetFoodDesc: Roasted peanuts coated in caramelised sugar, sold by street vendors.
AO.dessertDesc: A yellow pudding of grated coconut cooked with sugar, egg yolks and cinnamon.
AO.drinkDesc: A lightly fermented drink of maize flour, and Cuca, a long-established Angolan lager.

DZ.mainDish1Desc: Steamed semolina served with a broth of lamb or chicken, chickpeas, carrots, turnips and courgettes.
DZ.mainDish2Desc: Torn pieces of thin semolina flatbread soaked in a spicy tomato stew of lamb and chickpeas.
DZ.streetFoodDesc: A baked flan of chickpea flour, water, oil and cumin, served in a baguette with harissa.
DZ.dessertDesc: A semolina and almond cake soaked in orange-blossom syrup and cut into squares.
DZ.drinkDesc: Sweet green tea with fresh mint, and fermented buttermilk often served with couscous.

KY.mainDish1Desc: Stew of farmed green sea turtle meat simmered with onions, peppers, tomatoes and spices, long regarded as the Cayman Islands' national dish.
KY.mainDish2Desc: Fish cooked down in coconut milk with breadfruit, cassava, yam, onions and Scotch bonnet pepper.
KY.streetFoodDesc: Flaky turmeric-tinted pastry turnovers filled with spiced ground beef.
KY.dessertDesc: Dense cake of grated cassava or yam baked with coconut milk, brown sugar and spices.
KY.drinkDesc: The Mudslide cocktail of vodka, coffee liqueur and Irish cream, credited to Rum Point on Grand Cayman, and fruit-based rum punch.

CR.mainDish1Desc: Rice and black beans fried together with onion, sweet pepper, cilantro and Salsa Lizano, usually eaten at breakfast with eggs.
CR.mainDish2Desc: Lunch plate of rice, black beans, fried sweet plantains, cabbage salad and a choice of meat, chicken or fish.
CR.streetFoodDesc: Bowl of rice, beans and fried pork chicharrones topped with pico de gallo and served with tortilla chips.
CR.dessertDesc: Sponge cake soaked in evaporated milk, condensed milk and cream.
CR.drinkDesc: Highland-grown arabica coffee, and guaro, a clear sugarcane spirit.

CU.mainDish1Desc: Shredded flank steak braised in a sofrito of tomato, onion, peppers, garlic and cumin, served with rice.
CU.mainDish2Desc: Black beans and white rice cooked together with sofrito, bay leaf and cumin.
CU.streetFoodDesc: Roast pork marinated in mojo of sour orange and garlic, served in Cuban bread.
CU.dessertDesc: Puff pastry turnovers filled with guava paste, sometimes with cream cheese.
CU.drinkDesc: Rum muddled with mint, lime and sugar topped with soda water, and strong sweetened espresso.

DM.mainDish1Desc: Soup of dasheen leaves cooked with okra, coconut milk, pumpkin and seasonings, adopted as the national dish after mountain chicken became endangered.
DM.mainDish2Desc: Fritters made from titiri, tiny river fish fry, mixed into a seasoned flour batter and deep-fried.
DM.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds, often split and filled with saltfish or cheese.
DM.dessertDesc: Hard candy of grated coconut boiled with sugar and spices, then set in pieces.
DM.drinkDesc: Kubuli, the island's lager brewed with mountain spring water, and Macoucherie rum from a Dominica estate distillery.

DO.mainDish1Desc: Lunch plate of white rice, stewed red beans and braised chicken or beef, usually with salad and fried plantains.
DO.mainDish2Desc: Thick stew of several meats with yuca, plantain, yautía, corn and squash, served with rice and avocado.
DO.streetFoodDesc: Burger of seasoned ground meat on a soft bun with shredded cabbage, onion, tomato and a ketchup-mayonnaise sauce.
DO.dessertDesc: Sweet cream of red beans cooked with coconut milk, evaporated milk, sweet potato, raisins and spices, eaten during Lent.
DO.drinkDesc: Rum, red wine and honey steeped with tree bark and herbs, and Presidente lager.

SV.mainDish1Desc: Thick griddled corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, refried beans, chicharrón or loroco, served with curtido and tomato salsa.
SV.mainDish2Desc: Bread rolls filled with chicken or turkey braised in a spiced tomato sauce, with watercress, cucumber and radish.
SV.streetFoodDesc: Boiled then fried cassava served with fried pork pieces, curtido and tomato sauce.
SV.dessertDesc: Sweet pound cake made with rice flour, cheese and sour cream, topped with sesame seeds.
SV.drinkDesc: Horchata made from ground morro seeds, rice and spices, and Kolachampan, a sugarcane-flavoured soda.

GL.mainDish1Desc: Soup of seal, whale, reindeer or seabird meat boiled with onions and potatoes and thickened with rice or barley.
GL.mainDish2Desc: Raw whale skin with a layer of blubber, cut into small pieces and eaten as a delicacy.
GL.streetFoodDesc: Capelin dried in the open air and eaten as a snack, often with blubber.
GL.dessertDesc: Danish-style layered sponge cake with cream and berries, served at kaffemik home gatherings.
GL.drinkDesc: Flambéed coffee with whisky, coffee liqueur and Grand Marnier, topped with whipped cream.

GD.mainDish1Desc: One-pot dish of breadfruit, salted meat, chicken, dumplings and callaloo cooked in coconut milk with turmeric until the liquid is absorbed.
GD.mainDish2Desc: Tenderised conch stewed with onions, garlic, thyme, tomatoes and hot pepper.
GD.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough bakes served with sautéed salted cod, onions, tomatoes and peppers.
GD.dessertDesc: Ice cream flavoured with locally grown grated nutmeg.
GD.drinkDesc: Hot drink of local cocoa balls grated into milk with spices, and rum punch dusted with nutmeg.

GT.mainDish1Desc: Thick stew of chicken or beef in a sauce of toasted pumpkin and sesame seeds, dried chiles, tomatoes and tomatillos.
GT.mainDish2Desc: Q'eqchi' Maya turkey soup in a red broth of tomatoes, chiles, achiote and coriander.
GT.streetFoodDesc: Hot dogs in toasted buns topped with guacamole, boiled cabbage, mustard, ketchup and mayonnaise.
GT.dessertDesc: Mashed ripe plantain dough filled with sweetened black beans and chocolate, fried and dusted with sugar.
GT.drinkDesc: Warm, thick drink of fresh corn, milk, sugar and cinnamon, and highland-grown coffee.

HT.mainDish1Desc: Pork shoulder marinated in sour orange and epis, braised and then fried, served with pikliz and fried plantains.
HT.mainDish2Desc: Squash soup with beef, pasta, potatoes and vegetables, eaten on 1 January to mark independence.
HT.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried dough pastries filled with herring, chicken or ground beef.
HT.dessertDesc: Baked pudding of grated sweet potato, banana, coconut milk, raisins and spices.
HT.drinkDesc: Creamy drink of coconut milk, condensed milk, rum and spices, and Barbancourt rum.

HN.mainDish1Desc: Plate of grilled beef, refried red beans, rice, fried plantains, fresh cheese, cream and tortillas.
HN.mainDish2Desc: Conch soup cooked in coconut milk with green bananas, yuca, cilantro and spices.
HN.streetFoodDesc: Thick flour tortillas folded over refried beans, crumbled cheese and cream, often with egg or meat.
HN.dessertDesc: Slices of bread dipped in egg, fried and soaked in a spiced panela syrup, made for Holy Week.
HN.drinkDesc: Garifuna infusion of rum steeped with herbs and roots, and Salva Vida lager.

JM.mainDish1Desc: Boiled ackee fruit sautéed with salted cod, onions, tomatoes, Scotch bonnet pepper and thyme.
JM.mainDish2Desc: Chicken marinated in allspice, Scotch bonnet, scallion and thyme, then smoked over pimento wood.
JM.streetFoodDesc: Flaky golden turnover filled with spiced ground beef, often eaten in coco bread.
JM.dessertDesc: Pinched pastry tart filled with grated coconut cooked with brown sugar, nutmeg and ginger.
JM.drinkDesc: Coffee grown in the Blue Mountains, and sorrel, a hibiscus drink spiced with ginger and often spiked with rum.

MS.mainDish1Desc: Thick stew of goat meat with breadfruit, papaya, dumplings, cloves and hot pepper.
MS.mainDish2Desc: Boiled pork pieces pickled in a brine of lime juice, cucumber, onion and hot pepper.
MS.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds eaten plain or with saltfish.
MS.dessertDesc: Tamarind pulp rolled with sugar into sweet-sour balls.
MS.drinkDesc: Home-brewed spicy ginger beer, and rum punch mixed with fruit juices.

CW.mainDish1Desc: Hollowed Edam or Gouda cheese rind stuffed with spiced chicken, olives, raisins and capers, then baked.
CW.mainDish2Desc: Slow-cooked stew, most often of goat (kabritu), with tomatoes, peppers, cumin and cucumber, served with funchi.
CW.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried turnovers filled with cheese, spiced meat, chicken or tuna.
