CW.dessertDesc: Dark fruit cake of rum-soaked dried fruits, molasses and spices, made for weddings and holidays.
CW.drinkDesc: Orange liqueur made from dried laraha peels, and fresh limeade.

AW.mainDish1Desc: Baked Gouda or Edam cheese filled with spiced chicken or beef, olives, raisins and capers.
AW.mainDish2Desc: Fried whole fish served with Creole tomato and pepper sauce, funchi and pan bati.
AW.streetFoodDesc: Crescent-shaped fried pastries filled with cheese, ground meat, chicken or fish.
AW.dessertDesc: Sweets of grated coconut cooked with sugar and formed into small mounds.
AW.drinkDesc: Cocktail of vodka, rum, Coecoei liqueur and fruit juices, and Balashi lager brewed on the island.

SX.mainDish1Desc: Tenderised conch stewed in a seasoned broth with flour dumplings.
SX.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with pigeon peas, onions, thyme and often salted meat or coconut milk.
SX.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds, served with saltfish or cheese at breakfast.
SX.dessertDesc: Pastry tart filled with a jam of wild guavaberries.
SX.drinkDesc: Rum-based liqueur infused with wild guavaberries, the island's traditional Christmas drink.

NI.mainDish1Desc: Rice fried with small red beans, onion, sweet pepper and garlic, eaten with eggs, cheese and tortillas.
NI.mainDish2Desc: Large tamal of corn masa filled with pork, rice, potato, tomato and mint, wrapped in plantain leaves and boiled.
NI.streetFoodDesc: Boiled yuca topped with chicharrón and cabbage salad, served on a banana leaf.
NI.dessertDesc: Sponge cake soaked in rum syrup and topped with custard and cinnamon.
NI.drinkDesc: Flor de Caña aged rum, and pinolillo, a drink of toasted ground corn and cacao mixed with water or milk.

PA.mainDish1Desc: Chicken soup with ñame, oregano and culantro, served with white rice.
PA.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with chicken, sofrito, achiote, peas and olives.
PA.streetFoodDesc: Torpedo-shaped fritters of mashed yuca stuffed with seasoned ground beef.
PA.dessertDesc: Sponge cake soaked in a syrup of rum or wine with raisins and prunes.
PA.drinkDesc: Seco Herrerano, a clear sugarcane spirit, and chicha, a fruit juice drink.

PR.mainDish1Desc: Fried green plantains mashed in a pilón with garlic, olive oil and chicharrón, often served with broth or meat.
PR.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with pigeon peas, sofrito, pork and olives, coloured with annatto.
PR.streetFoodDesc: Fritters of grated green banana and yautía dough stuffed with seasoned ground beef or crab.
PR.dessertDesc: Coconut milk pudding set with cornstarch and dusted with cinnamon.
PR.drinkDesc: Blended rum, coconut cream and pineapple, and coquito, a Christmas coconut-rum eggnog.

BL.mainDish1Desc: Local spiny lobster split and grilled, served with lime and Creole sauce.
BL.mainDish2Desc: Fish poached in a broth of tomatoes, onions, garlic, lime, thyme and hot pepper.
BL.streetFoodDesc: Spiced blood sausage seasoned with hot pepper, chives and lime.
BL.dessertDesc: Baked custard of eggs, coconut milk and condensed milk with caramel.
BL.drinkDesc: Rhum agricole stirred with lime and cane syrup.

KN.mainDish1Desc: Salted cod stewed with tomatoes, onions and peppers, served with spicy plantains, coconut dumplings and seasoned breadfruit.
KN.mainDish2Desc: Goat meat stew seasoned with cloves, thyme and hot pepper, often with dumplings.
KN.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds, often filled with saltfish.
KN.dessertDesc: Candy of grated coconut boiled with sugar and coloured syrup, set in small mounds.
KN.drinkDesc: Clear spirit distilled from sugarcane juice on St. Kitts, usually mixed with Ting grapefruit soda.

AI.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked with pigeon peas, onions, thyme and salted meat, served with fried or stewed fish.
AI.mainDish2Desc: Anguillan spiny lobster ('crayfish') split and grilled with butter, garlic and lime.
AI.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds eaten with saltfish or fried fish.
AI.dessertDesc: Pastry tart filled with grated coconut cooked with sugar and spices.
AI.drinkDesc: Local rum mixed with fruit juices, grenadine and nutmeg.

LC.mainDish1Desc: Boiled unripe bananas ('green figs') served with salted cod sautéed with onions, peppers and herbs.
LC.mainDish2Desc: Hearty one-pot soup of red beans, ground provisions, dumplings and meat such as pig tail or chicken.
LC.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried fritters of salted cod in a seasoned flour batter with herbs and hot pepper.
LC.dessertDesc: Baked pastry turnovers filled with grated coconut cooked with sugar and spices.
LC.drinkDesc: Grated local cocoa sticks boiled with milk, cinnamon and nutmeg, and Piton lager.

MF.mainDish1Desc: Chicken curry made with colombo spice powder, garlic, lime, christophine and potatoes, served with rice.
MF.mainDish2Desc: Fried dough rounds served with salted cod sautéed with onions, tomatoes and peppers.
MF.streetFoodDesc: Small fritters of salted cod, herbs and hot pepper in a light batter.
MF.dessertDesc: Chilled coconut milk pudding set with gelatin, often served with fruit coulis.
MF.drinkDesc: Guavaberry rum liqueur, and ti' punch of rhum agricole, lime and cane syrup.

PM.mainDish1Desc: Cod stew with potatoes and onions, a traditional dish of the islands' fishing families.
PM.mainDish2Desc: Scallops from local waters baked in their shells with a creamy sauce and breadcrumbs.
PM.streetFoodDesc: Fried cakes of salted cod mixed with mashed potato and herbs.
PM.dessertDesc: Tart filled with cloudberries, called plaquebières locally.
PM.drinkDesc: Rum, tied to the islands' Prohibition-era trade, and wine imported from France.

VC.mainDish1Desc: Whole breadfruit roasted over coals, peeled and served with seasoned fried jackfish.
VC.mainDish2Desc: Soup of dasheen leaves with okra, coconut milk, dumplings and salted meat.
VC.streetFoodDesc: Flatbread wrapped around curried chicken, goat or vegetables with potato.
VC.dessertDesc: Dark Christmas cake of dried fruits soaked in rum and wine, browned sugar and spices.
VC.drinkDesc: Sunset Very Strong overproof rum, and Hairoun lager, both produced on St. Vincent.

TT.mainDish1Desc: Thick purée of dasheen leaves, okra, pumpkin and coconut milk, often cooked with crab and salted meat.
TT.mainDish2Desc: One-pot dish of rice, pigeon peas and chicken browned in caramelised sugar, cooked with coconut milk and green seasoning.
TT.streetFoodDesc: Two pieces of fried bara bread filled with curried chickpeas and topped with tamarind and cucumber chutneys and pepper sauce.
TT.dessertDesc: Crunchy fried strips of spiced dough coated in a ginger-flavoured sugar syrup.
TT.drinkDesc: Bittersweet drink from mauby tree bark boiled with spices, and Carib lager.

TC.mainDish1Desc: Hominy grits cooked with pigeon peas, salt pork, onions and tomato, served with conch or fish.
TC.mainDish2Desc: Tenderised conch, battered and deep-fried, served with lime and dipping sauce.
TC.streetFoodDesc: Raw diced conch marinated in lime and orange juice with onion, sweet pepper, tomato and hot pepper.
TC.dessertDesc: Pastry tart filled with sweetened grated coconut.
TC.drinkDesc: Turk's Head lager brewed on Providenciales, and Bambarra rum.

VI.mainDish1Desc: Boiled or stewed fish in a seasoned tomato and onion sauce, served with fungi, a cornmeal and okra mash.
VI.mainDish2Desc: Stew of local greens with okra, salted meat, seafood and hot pepper, served with fungi.
VI.streetFoodDesc: Fried pastry turnovers filled with spiced beef, saltfish or chicken.
VI.dessertDesc: Pudding of guava or other fruit thickened with tapioca or sago, a dish of Danish colonial origin.
VI.drinkDesc: Fermented drink of mauby bark, ginger and spices, and rum distilled on St. Croix.

BM.mainDish1Desc: Dark, spicy soup of fish, tomatoes, onions and vegetables, finished with black rum and sherry peppers sauce.
BM.mainDish2Desc: Sunday breakfast of boiled salt cod and potatoes with tomato-onion sauce, avocado, banana and hard-boiled egg.
BM.streetFoodDesc: Fried fillet of local fish on raisin bread with coleslaw, tartar sauce and hot sauce.
BM.dessertDesc: Bundt-style butter cake soaked in a black rum glaze.
BM.drinkDesc: Rum shaken with fruit juices and falernum, and Gosling's black rum with ginger beer.

VG.mainDish1Desc: Seasoned stewed or fried fish served with fungi, a cornmeal and okra mash.
VG.mainDish2Desc: Tenderised conch stewed with onions, peppers, tomatoes and herbs.
VG.streetFoodDesc: Fried pastries filled with saltfish, beef or chicken.
VG.dessertDesc: Pastry tart filled with grated coconut cooked with sugar and spices.
VG.drinkDesc: Dark rum with pineapple juice, orange juice and cream of coconut topped with nutmeg, created on Jost Van Dyke.

BZ.mainDish1Desc: Rice cooked with red kidney beans and coconut milk, served with stewed chicken, potato salad and fried plantains.
BZ.mainDish2Desc: Garifuna dish of fish cooked in a coconut milk broth, served with mashed green and ripe plantains.
BZ.streetFoodDesc: Crisp fried corn tortillas topped with refried beans, grated cheese and pickled onions.
BZ.dessertDesc: Baked pudding of grated sweet potato with coconut milk, sugar, ginger and nutmeg.
BZ.drinkDesc: Belikin beer, and a blended drink of seaweed, milk, condensed milk and nutmeg.

BB.mainDish1Desc: Cornmeal and okra stirred into a smooth mash, served with flying fish steamed in a tomato, onion and herb sauce.
BB.mainDish2Desc: Steamed sweet potato pudding served with pork pickled in lime juice, cucumber, onion and hot pepper.
BB.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried fritters of salt cod, herbs and hot pepper, often served in a salt bread 'bread and two'.
BB.dessertDesc: Cornmeal, pumpkin, sweet potato, coconut and raisins steamed in banana leaves.
BB.drinkDesc: Rum punch made with Barbadian rum, lime and nutmeg, and bittersweet mauby bark drink.

BS.mainDish1Desc: Tenderised conch, battered and deep-fried, served with peas 'n' rice and lime.
BS.mainDish2Desc: Fish boiled with onions, potatoes, lime, celery and hot pepper, served with johnnycake for breakfast.
BS.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried balls of chopped conch in a seasoned batter with peppers and onions.
BS.dessertDesc: Dough rolled around guava pulp, steamed or boiled, and served with a sweet butter-rum sauce.
BS.drinkDesc: Rum cocktail with coconut rum and pineapple juice, and sky juice of gin, coconut water and condensed milk.

AG.mainDish1Desc: Cornmeal and okra mash served with pepperpot, a thick stew of salted meat, greens, eggplant, okra and squash.
AG.mainDish2Desc: Grated sweet potato and coconut dumplings boiled in banana leaves, served with stewed saltfish.
AG.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough rounds eaten with saltfish or cheese.
AG.dessertDesc: Candy of grated coconut boiled with sugar and set into small pieces.
AG.drinkDesc: Aged rum from the Antigua Distillery, and Wadadli lager.

CL.mainDish1Desc: Baked casserole of ground beef, onions, chicken, olives and egg topped with a sweetened purée of fresh corn and basil.
CL.mainDish2Desc: Clear broth with a piece of beef or chicken, potato, squash, corn on the cob and rice.
CL.streetFoodDesc: Hot dog in a large bun topped with tomato, avocado, mayonnaise and sauerkraut.
CL.dessertDesc: Baked custard of milk, eggs and sugar with a browned top and caramel.
CL.drinkDesc: Pisco shaken with lemon juice, sugar and egg white, and Carménère red wine.

EC.mainDish1Desc: Albacore tuna soup with yuca and pickled red onions, seasoned with cumin and cilantro and served with plantain chips.
EC.mainDish2Desc: Creamy potato soup with cheese and achiote, topped with avocado.
EC.streetFoodDesc: Ball of mashed fried green plantain mixed with cheese or pork cracklings.
EC.dessertDesc: Fruit sorbet spun by hand in a copper pan set over ice.
EC.drinkDesc: Hot cinnamon and naranjilla drink spiked with aguardiente, and a spiced purple corn and fruit drink made for the Day of the Dead.

FK.mainDish1Desc: Roast leg or shoulder of locally raised mutton, the main meat of the islands' sheep farms.
FK.mainDish2Desc: Squid from the islands' Loligo fishery, typically battered and fried as calamari.
FK.streetFoodDesc: Battered fried local fish served with chips.
FK.dessertDesc: Jam made from the red berries of the diddle-dee shrub, eaten on scones and in tarts.
FK.drinkDesc: British-style tea with milk, served at the morning and afternoon 'smoko' breaks.

GY.mainDish1Desc: Amerindian-origin stew of beef or pork slow-cooked in cassareep with cinnamon, cloves and wiri wiri pepper, eaten at Christmas with bread.
GY.mainDish2Desc: One-pot rice cooked with black-eyed peas, coconut milk, salted meat and chicken.
GY.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried balls of spiced split pea batter served with mango or tamarind sour.
GY.dessertDesc: Sweet bread roll filled with red-coloured sweetened grated coconut.
GY.drinkDesc: Demerara rum from the El Dorado distillery, and bittersweet mauby bark drink.

PY.mainDish1Desc: Savoury cornbread made with cornmeal, cheese, onions, milk and eggs, baked until firm.
PY.mainDish2Desc: Baked pudding of fresh ground corn, cheese, onions, milk and eggs.
PY.streetFoodDesc: Ring-shaped baked rolls of cassava starch, cheese and anise.
PY.dessertDesc: Bitter orange peel candied in black molasses.
PY.drinkDesc: Yerba mate steeped in iced water or fruit juice with crushed medicinal herbs.

SR.mainDish1Desc: Oven dish of grated pomtajer root layered with chicken stewed with citrus, onion and tomato.
SR.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with a mix of salted meat, fish, beans and vegetables.
SR.streetFoodDesc: Deep-fried dough rings of split pea flour, served with pepper sauce or as a sandwich.
SR.dessertDesc: Baked cake of grated cassava, coconut, raisins and sugar.
SR.drinkDesc: Borgoe rum from Suriname's SAB distillery, and Parbo lager.

UY.mainDish1Desc: Sandwich of thin grilled beef steak with ham, mozzarella, bacon, fried egg, lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise.
UY.mainDish2Desc: Beef cuts, sausages and offal grilled slowly on a parrilla over wood embers.
UY.streetFoodDesc: Fried dough discs, traditionally eaten on rainy days with mate.
UY.dessertDesc: Paysandú cake of sponge layered with meringue, cream and peaches.
UY.drinkDesc: Yerba mate infusion drunk through a bombilla, and Tannat red wine.

VE.mainDish1Desc: Plate of shredded stewed beef, black beans, white rice and fried ripe plantains.
VE.mainDish2Desc: Grilled pre-cooked cornmeal patties split and filled with cheese, shredded beef, black beans or chicken-avocado salad.
VE.streetFoodDesc: Sticks of white cheese wrapped in wheat dough and deep-fried.
VE.dessertDesc: Caramel-topped custard of eggs and condensed milk.
VE.drinkDesc: Drink of dissolved raw cane sugar and lime juice, and aged Venezuelan rum.

BO.mainDish1Desc: Baked pastries filled with a juicy stew of beef or chicken, potatoes, peas, olives, egg and spices.
BO.mainDish2Desc: Platter of bite-sized beef and sausage over fries, topped with onions, tomatoes, locoto peppers and boiled egg.
BO.streetFoodDesc: Skewers of grilled beef heart marinated in ají and served with potatoes and peanut sauce.
BO.dessertDesc: Fried dough fritters drizzled with syrup, often eaten with hot api.
BO.drinkDesc: Hot, thick purple corn drink spiced with cinnamon and cloves, and singani, a grape brandy.

CK.mainDish1Desc: Raw reef fish or tuna cubed and marinated in lime or lemon juice, then mixed with coconut cream, tomato, cucumber and onion.
CK.mainDish2Desc: Young taro leaves cooked slowly with coconut cream and onion until soft.
CK.streetFoodDesc: Cook Islands potato salad with mayonnaise, often served beside barbecue plates at Punanga Nui market and feasts.
CK.dessertDesc: Pudding of ripe banana or pawpaw mixed with arrowroot starch, baked and served with coconut cream.
CK.drinkDesc: Drinking coconut, and Atiu's tumunu bush beer brewed in a hollowed coconut-tree stump and shared in a drinking circle.

FJ.mainDish1Desc: Raw white fish marinated in lime juice and mixed with coconut cream, chili, tomato and onion, often served in a coconut shell.
FJ.mainDish2Desc: Pork, chicken, fish, cassava and taro wrapped in banana leaves and cooked on hot stones in an earth oven.
FJ.streetFoodDesc: Indo-Fijian curry of chicken, goat or vegetables wrapped in a soft roti.
FJ.dessertDesc: Grated cassava mixed with coconut cream and sugar, wrapped in banana leaves and baked.
FJ.drinkDesc: Ceremonial drink made from pounded yaqona root mixed with water and served from a wooden tanoa bowl.

PF.mainDish1Desc: Raw tuna cubed and marinated in lime juice, then mixed with coconut milk, tomato, cucumber and onion.
PF.mainDish2Desc: Chicken simmered with young taro leaves (fafa) in coconut milk.
PF.streetFoodDesc: Chinese-Tahitian stir-fried noodles with pork, vegetables and sauce, sold from the roulottes (food trucks) of Papeete.
PF.dessertDesc: Baked pudding of puréed fruit such as banana, papaya or pumpkin with starch, served with coconut milk.
PF.drinkDesc: Hinano lager brewed in Tahiti, and fresh drinking coconut.

KI.mainDish1Desc: Giant swamp taro grown in dug-out pits, boiled or baked and often mashed with coconut cream and coconut syrup for feasts.
KI.mainDish2Desc: Large land crab cooked whole by boiling or roasting and eaten with coconut cream.
KI.streetFoodDesc: Thin slices of breadfruit deep-fried until crisp.
KI.dessertDesc: Dried pandanus-fruit flour eaten mixed with water or coconut, a traditional preserved food of the atolls.
KI.drinkDesc: Fresh sweet sap tapped from coconut flower spathes; when boiled down it becomes kamaimai syrup.

GU.mainDish1Desc: Chamorro dish of chopped grilled chicken, shrimp or fish 'cooked' in lemon juice with grated coconut, green onion and hot donne' peppers.
GU.mainDish2Desc: Rice cooked with achote (annatto) seeds that colour it red, served at every Chamorro fiesta.
GU.streetFoodDesc: Fried half-moon pastry with an achote-tinted crust filled with a toasted rice and coconut cream mixture.
GU.dessertDesc: Sponge cake topped with a thick vanilla custard and dusted with cinnamon.
GU.drinkDesc: Coconut toddy made from the sap of the coconut flower, drunk fresh or fermented.

NR.mainDish1Desc: Fish fillets, often tuna, coated in grated coconut and fried, a common Nauruan home dish.
NR.mainDish2Desc: Black noddy terns caught at dusk with hand nets along the coast, plucked and fried or roasted as a traditional delicacy.
NR.streetFoodDesc: Fried rice with egg and meat from the Chinese-run takeaway shops that supply much of Nauru's everyday food.
NR.dessertDesc: Ripe pandanus keys chewed raw for their sweet, fibrous pulp.
NR.drinkDesc: Sap tapped from coconut flower stalks, drunk fresh or fermented.

NC.mainDish1Desc: Kanak dish of yam, taro, sweet potato and banana layered with chicken, fish or crab, doused in coconut milk, wrapped in banana leaves and cooked on hot stones.
NC.mainDish2Desc: Rusa deer venison stewed in red wine with onions and spices, a staple of the Caledonian bush.
NC.streetFoodDesc: Javanese-style fried noodles with vegetables and meat, sold in snack bars across Nouméa.
NC.dessertDesc: Baked custard made with coconut milk, eggs and sugar.
NC.drinkDesc: Number One lager brewed in Nouméa, and kava drunk in the city's nakamal bars.

VU.mainDish1Desc: Grated yam, taro, manioc or banana pounded into a paste, topped with coconut cream and meat or fish, wrapped in leaves and baked in an earth oven.
VU.mainDish2Desc: Grated manioc or banana rolled in island cabbage leaves and simmered in coconut cream.
VU.streetFoodDesc: Grated manioc dough filled with seasoned pork, wrapped in leaves and cooked, sold at Port Vila market.
VU.dessertDesc: Canarium nuts eaten roasted or fresh and pounded into puddings during the nut season.
VU.drinkDesc: Strong root drink prepared fresh and drunk at dusk in village and town nakamals.

NZ.mainDish1Desc: Māori earth-oven feast of lamb, pork, chicken, kūmara, potato and pumpkin steamed for hours on heated stones under the ground.
NZ.mainDish2Desc: Leg of lamb roasted with rosemary and garlic and served with roast potatoes, kūmara and mint sauce.
NZ.streetFoodDesc: Flaky pastry pie filled with minced beef in gravy and melted cheese.
NZ.dessertDesc: Meringue dessert with a crisp shell and soft centre, topped with whipped cream and kiwifruit or berries.
NZ.drinkDesc: Espresso with velvety steamed milk, and Marlborough's Sauvignon Blanc white wine.

NU.mainDish1Desc: Layers of sliced taro and pawpaw covered in coconut cream, wrapped in leaves and baked in an umu.
NU.mainDish2Desc: Large land crab boiled or baked and eaten with coconut cream, a prized Niuean delicacy.
NU.streetFoodDesc: Raw fish marinated in citrus juice and mixed with coconut cream and vegetables.
NU.dessertDesc: Baked pudding of flour and ripe banana or pumpkin enriched with coconut cream.
NU.drinkDesc: Fresh drinking coconut, and juice of the noni fruit produced on the island.

NF.mainDish1Desc: Pie of periwinkles (hihi) gathered from the island's rocks, cooked with onion and bacon under a pastry crust.
NF.mainDish2Desc: Baked dish of grated green banana, kumara or pumpkin mixed with flour and coconut or milk, inherited from Tahitian forebears.
NF.streetFoodDesc: Dumplings of grated green banana boiled and served with butter or coconut sauce.
NF.dessertDesc: Jam made from the cherry guava that grows wild across Norfolk Island.
NF.drinkDesc: Arabica coffee grown and roasted in small quantities on the island.

MP.mainDish1Desc: Grilled chicken chopped and mixed with lemon juice, grated coconut, green onion and hot peppers.
MP.mainDish2Desc: Coconut crab steamed or cooked in coconut milk, served at fiestas.
MP.streetFoodDesc: Chamorro flatbread made with flour or corn, coconut milk and sugar, cooked on a griddle.
MP.dessertDesc: Grated young coconut and tapioca starch wrapped in banana leaves and grilled.
MP.drinkDesc: Coconut toddy made from coconut flower sap, drunk fresh or fermented.

FM.mainDish1Desc: Chuukese pounded breadfruit or taro, often mixed with coconut cream and eaten at gatherings.
FM.mainDish2Desc: Slices of raw yellowfin tuna eaten with soy sauce and hot mustard or lemon, a legacy of the Japanese era.
FM.streetFoodDesc: Thin slices of breadfruit deep-fried until crisp.
FM.dessertDesc: Small orange-fleshed Pohnpeian banana eaten ripe or cooked, valued for its sweetness.
FM.drinkDesc: Pohnpeian kava made by pounding kava root on stone and squeezing it through hibiscus bark.

MH.mainDish1Desc: Breadfruit fermented in leaf-lined pits into a preserved paste, then wrapped in leaves and baked.
MH.mainDish2Desc: Coconut crab boiled or baked and eaten with rice and coconut.
MH.streetFoodDesc: Thin slices of breadfruit deep-fried until crisp.
MH.dessertDesc: Sweet paste of cooked pandanus pulp dried in the sun, a traditional preserved food for long voyages.
MH.drinkDesc: Fresh sap tapped from coconut flower spathes, drunk sweet or boiled into jekmai syrup.

PW.mainDish1Desc: Whole fruit bat simmered with coconut milk, ginger and onion, served at special occasions.
PW.mainDish2Desc: Taro leaves cooked with crab or fish in coconut milk.
PW.streetFoodDesc: Slices of raw tuna served with soy sauce and wasabi, a legacy of Japanese rule.
PW.dessertDesc: Fried dough balls eaten as a sweet snack.
PW.drinkDesc: Drink made from coconut syrup diluted with water.

PG.mainDish1Desc: Earth-oven feast of pork, kaukau (sweet potato), taro, banana and greens wrapped in banana leaves and cooked on hot stones.
PG.mainDish2Desc: Sago starch dumplings mixed with banana and boiled in coconut cream, eaten in the Sepik and other lowland areas.
PG.streetFoodDesc: Fatty mutton flaps grilled or fried and sold at markets and roadside stalls.
PG.dessertDesc: Canarium nuts from East New Britain eaten raw, roasted or as nut bars.
PG.drinkDesc: Green drinking coconut, and arabica coffee grown in the Highlands.

PN.mainDish1Desc: Baked dish of grated banana, kumara or pumpkin mixed with flour and coconut milk, from the islanders' Tahitian heritage.
PN.mainDish2Desc: Pitkern name for the drummer fish caught off the island's rocks, usually fried.
PN.streetFoodDesc: Sun-dried bananas made by islanders and sold to passing ships and by mail order.
PN.dessertDesc: Honey from the island's disease-free bee population, eaten on bread or in baking.
PN.drinkDesc: Fresh drinking coconut from the island's palms.

TO.mainDish1Desc: Corned beef and onion wrapped in taro leaves with coconut cream, then baked in an umu.
TO.mainDish2Desc: Raw fish marinated in lemon or lime juice and mixed with coconut cream, tomato, cucumber and onion.
TO.streetFoodDesc: Tongan doughnut balls, often made with banana, deep-fried and sold at markets.
TO.dessertDesc: Dumplings of taro, breadfruit or flour drenched in caramelised coconut syrup.
TO.drinkDesc: Kava root drink shared at evening faikava gatherings and ceremonies.

WF.mainDish1Desc: Taro leaves filled with corned beef or fish and coconut cream, wrapped and baked in the umu.
WF.mainDish2Desc: Whole pig, yam, taro and breadfruit cooked on hot stones in an earth oven for feasts and church celebrations.
WF.streetFoodDesc: Raw fish marinated in lime juice and mixed with coconut milk and vegetables.
WF.dessertDesc: Taro or breadfruit dumplings coated in caramelised coconut syrup.
WF.drinkDesc: Kava root drink prepared for ceremonies and royal custom gatherings.

WS.mainDish1Desc: Young taro leaves filled with thick coconut cream and onion, wrapped and baked in an umu.
WS.mainDish2Desc: Raw fish marinated in lemon juice and mixed with coconut cream, tomato, cucumber and onion.
WS.streetFoodDesc: Round Samoan doughnuts, sometimes made with banana, deep-fried and sold at markets.
WS.dessertDesc: Soft buns baked in a sweet coconut cream sauce.
WS.drinkDesc: Drink made from roasted local cocoa beans with sugar and water, and ceremonial ʻava (kava).

AS.mainDish1Desc: Taro leaves filled with coconut cream and onion, wrapped and baked in an umu.
AS.mainDish2Desc: Samoan chop suey of glass noodles stir-fried with chicken or beef, soy sauce, ginger and garlic.
AS.dessertDesc: Cubes of taro covered in caramelised coconut cream.
AS.drinkDesc: Drink made from roasted cocoa beans pounded into paste and mixed with sugar and hot water.

SB.mainDish1Desc: Pork, fish, root crops and leaf-wrapped puddings cooked on hot stones in an earth oven for feasts.
SB.mainDish2Desc: Leafy greens (Abelmoschus manihot) simmered in coconut milk, often with fish.
SB.streetFoodDesc: Canarium nuts eaten fresh or roasted, sold at Honiara Central Market.
SB.dessertDesc: Grated cassava mixed with coconut cream, wrapped in leaves and baked.
SB.drinkDesc: SolBrew lager brewed in Honiara, and fresh drinking coconut.

N. Cyprus.mainDish1Desc: Minced lamb seasoned with onion and parsley, wrapped in caul fat and grilled over charcoal, served in pitta with salad.
N. Cyprus.mainDish2Desc: Jute mallow leaves stewed slowly with lamb or chicken, tomato and lemon.
N. Cyprus.streetFoodDesc: Savoury bread or pastry baked with halloumi, black olives and dried mint.
N. Cyprus.dessertDesc: Fried filo parcels filled with a semolina custard, dusted with icing sugar.
N. Cyprus.drinkDesc: A chilled salted yoghurt drink, and strong unfiltered coffee served in small cups.
